title: 恋爱结婚效率为上？日本单身年轻人走进婚介所
description: RIVER AKIRA DAVIS, KIUKO NOTOYA2026年9月30日IBJ婚介服务的客户安田泰然走在东京街头。“我认为这将是找到有结婚这个相同目标者的最快方式，”他说。 Noriko Hayashi for The New York Times True love may be priceless. But in Japan, 20-somethings are flocking to marriage agencies that promise a fast track to the altar — and charge a premium for it. 真爱可能是无价的。但在日本，二十多岁的年轻人正涌向婚姻介绍所，这些机构承诺提供通往婚姻殿堂的捷径，并为此收取高额费用。 For hundreds of years, through the post-World War II era, Japanese marriages were brokered through “omiai,” a practice in which matchmakers — usually relatives, family friends or bosses — linked singles in their orbit. But the custom fell out of fashion, giving way to organic dating and, eventually, a wave of casual-dating apps. 直至二战后时期，数百年来日本的婚姻都是通过“相亲”来撮合的，根据这种习俗，媒人——通常是亲戚、世交或老板——为身边的单身人士牵线搭桥。但这种习俗后来不再流行，取而代之的是顺其自然的约会，最终被休闲约会应用的浪潮取代。 Now, young adults are enrolling at record rates in marriage agencies, where counselors serve as professional matchmakers. Across Tokyo, advertisements line metro cars, urging commuters to “leave life’s fateful encounters to the pros.” Another declares: “Better one omiai than 100 swipes.” 如今，年轻人正以创纪录的比例在婚姻介绍所注册，那里的顾问担任着专业媒人的角色。在整个东京，地铁车厢里布满了广告，敦促通勤者“把人生中注定的相遇交给专业人士”。另一则广告宣称：“一次相亲胜过滑动屏幕一百次。” Experts say the shift is being driven by a backlash against frustrations familiar to modern daters globally. With social circles shrinking, young Japanese — tired of the ghosting, catfishing and noncommittal matches rampant on dating apps — are turning to hands-on human guidance for greater efficiency and assurance. 专家表示，种转变源于全球现代约会者对常见挫折感的一种反噬。随着社交圈的缩小，日本年轻人厌倦了在约会应用上泛滥的“玩失踪”、网络身份造假和不愿承诺的配对——正转向需要亲力亲为的人工指导，以获得更高的效率和保障。 Among the new recruits was Taizen Yasuda. A soft-spoken 28-year-old, he said he had run out of patience for algorithm-driven romance. 安田泰然（音）就是这些新注册者中的一员。这位说话轻声细语的28岁年轻人表示，他对算法驱动的恋爱已经失去了耐心。 “The process of endless matching, messaging and finally meeting on apps was exhausting,” Mr. Yasuda said. Matchmaking services, he thought, “would be the quickest way to find someone with the exact same goal — marriage.” “在交友软件上无休止地匹配、发信息，最后见面，这个过程令人筋疲力尽，”安田泰然说。他认为，相亲服务“将是找到有着结婚这个相同目标者的最快方式”。 The practice is resurging as Japan grapples with a shrinking population and fewer young families. Because childbearing in Japan remains overwhelmingly tied to marriage, encouraging more people to wed has become part of the country’s broader push to boost its birthrate. 随着日本努力应对人口萎缩和年轻家庭减少的问题，这种做法正在复苏。由于在日本，生育仍然绝大程度上与婚姻挂钩，因此鼓励更多人结婚已成为该国提高出生率的更广泛举措的一部分。 28岁的安田泰然与他的IBJ顾问在一起。他表示，他很感谢通过顾问转达的约会对象的反馈意见。 Noriko Hayashi for The New York Times One company has positioned itself at the center of the matchmaking trend: IBJ, a Tokyo-based giant with a nationwide network. Promising to take clients from first meeting to proposal in three months, the company has seen membership and profits soar. It now claims a hand in roughly one of every 25 marriages in Japan. 一家公司将自己定位在这一相亲趋势的中心：总部位于东京、拥有全国性网络的巨头IBJ。这家公司承诺在三个月内让客户从初次见面走向求婚，其会员数量和利润都在飙升。该公司目前声称，日本大约每25场婚姻中就有一场是他们撮合的。 Mr. Yasuda is part of a wave of young singles who have joined IBJ. On a recent Sunday, he sat across from his counselor in a quiet consultation room, clad in a stiffly pressed suit, with a sweep of wavy hair combed to the side. A little over a month after joining the matchmaking service, Mr. Yasuda had already narrowed his prospects to two women. He had just taken one on a weekend drive to see a field of yellow canola blooms. 安田泰然是加入IBJ的年轻单身人士中的一员。在最近的一个周日，他坐在安静的咨询室里，坐在顾问的对面，穿着笔挺的西装，梳着偏分的卷发。在加入这项相亲服务一个多月后，安田泰然已经将潜在对象缩小到两名女性。他刚刚带了其中一位在周末自驾出游，欣赏一片盛开的黄色油菜花田。 Every member is assigned a consultant who micromanages the courtship process. The consultants advise on everything from grooming and messaging etiquette to date itineraries. 每位会员都会被分配一位顾问，负责细致管理整个求偶过程。顾问会就各方面提供建议，从仪容打扮、发信息礼仪到约会行程。 When two members match, their consultants work in tandem behind the scenes, doing what they call “Cupid work” — exchanging and filtering postdate feedback and helping orchestrate every milestone, down to an eventual proposal. 当两名成员匹配成功时，他们的顾问会在幕后协同工作，做他们所说的“丘比特工作”——交流和筛选约会后的反馈，协助安排每一个重要节点，直至最终的求婚。 “We are providing the kind of support only humans can offer to help people get married as quickly as possible,” said Shigeru Ishizaka, IBJ’s chief executive. “我们提供只有人类才能提供的那种支持，帮助人们尽快结婚，”IBJ首席执行官石坂茂表示。 IBJ的顾问畑惠子就方方面面提供建议，从仪容仪表、短信礼仪到约会行程安排。 In an increasingly digitized society, “there is a deep desire to have a person guiding you through the process of dating,” said Junko Yamada, a lecturer at Tokai University in Tokyo who studies the psychology of romance. Echoing the reassurance of traditional omiai, she said having an expert curate matches offered psychological safety. 在一个日益数字化的社会中，“人们内心深处渴望有人能在约会过程中提供指导，”在东京东海大学研究恋爱心理学的讲师山田顺子说。她表示，与传统相亲带来的安心感相应，由专家来精心挑选匹配对象能提供心理安全感。 Ms. Yamada said that today’s youths seemed fixated on maximizing efficiency in every aspect of their lives, and that these agencies appealed to that mind-set by filtering out people who weren’t serious about marriage. 山田顺子说，如今的年轻人似乎追求在生活的方方面面实现效率最大化，而这些机构通过过滤掉那些对婚姻不认真的对象，迎合了这种心态。 IBJ’s network of affiliated marriage agencies has varying costs and eligibility rules. Members typically pay about $30 to $100 a month, an enrollment fee of $650 to $1,300 and an additional $1,300 “success fee” if a couple get engaged. It also charges a $1,300 fee if couples violate its rules against “banned activities,” including premarital sex and cohabitation. IBJ said its counselors tracked the progression of their clients’ relationships. IBJ附属婚姻介绍所网络有着不同的收费标准和资格规定。会员通常每月支付约30至100美元，注册费为650至1300美元，如果两人订婚，还需额外支付1300美元的“成功费”。如果情侣违反该机构关于“禁止活动”（包括婚前性行为和同居）的规定，该机构还会收取1300美元的罚金。IBJ表示，其顾问会跟踪客户关系的发展。 Enrollment is generally limited to applicants with steady incomes. IBJ’s largest directly operated agency accepts only women ages 20 to 39 and men ages 25 to 49. 注册通常仅限于有稳定收入的申请人。IBJ最大的直营机构只接受20至39岁的女性和25至49岁的男性。 Critics argue that corporate services like IBJ, a company listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange with annual revenue exceeding $130 million, strip the soul from traditional matchmaking, impose rigid timelines on anxious young adults and turn dating into a moneymaking endeavor. 批评人士认为，像IBJ这样的企业化婚介服务剥夺了传统相亲的灵魂，给焦虑的年轻人强加了死板的时间表，将约会变成了一项赚钱的生意。IBJ已在东京证券交易所上市，年收入超过1.3亿美元。 “现代婚介机构做不到我做的事，”东京附近的一位资深婚介人加藤郁子说。 Among the skeptics is Ikuko Kato, a veteran matchmaker who operates from her lace-curtained home just outside Tokyo, filled with hundreds of smiling pictures of couples she has matched. Dressed in pearls and a pink knit suit, Ms. Kato said she had matched more than 1,300 couples over 44 years and claimed that not a single pair had divorced. 加藤郁子（音）就是这些怀疑者之一。这位资深媒人经营着一家家庭式婚介所，它位于东京郊外、挂着蕾丝窗帘，里面摆满了数百张她撮合的情侣的照片，每个人都笑容满面。加藤郁子戴着珍珠项链，穿着粉色针织套装，她说自己在44年里撮合了1300多对情侣，而且没有一对离婚。 “They’re too focused on business,” said Ms. Kato, who also charges clients a monthly fee as well as a fee if her matchmaking results in marriage. “My parents were neighborhood matchmakers. It’s in my blood. Modern corporate agents cannot do what I do.” “它们太注重商业了，”加藤郁子说，她也向客户收取月费，如果相亲成功结婚也会收取一笔费用。“我的父母就是街坊邻里间的媒人。这融入了我的血液。现代的企业婚介机构做不了我做的事情。” Unlike neighborhood matchmakers, IBJ moves clients through a lucrative, end-to-end program. Beyond matchmaking, its group companies offer wedding planning, financial consulting and housing services, along with referrals to affiliated businesses like eyebrow-grooming salons. 与邻里间的媒人不一样，IBJ为客户提供一条高利润的端到端服务流程。除了相亲，其集团公司还提供婚礼策划、财务咨询和住房服务，还会将客户推荐给修眉沙龙等合作商家。 Membership has grown about 50 percent over the past five years, and IBJ reported a 44 percent jump in first-half revenue this year, to about $91 million. 过去五年里，其会员人数增长了约50%，IBJ报告称，今年上半年的收入激增了44%，达到约9100万美元。 加藤郁子的家中挂满了她牵线搭桥的1300多对情侣的照片。她声称，这些情侣中没有一对离婚。 Mr. Ishizaka, the chief executive, said he viewed IBJ’s mission as more than just money. When he left banking and entered the matchmaking industry in 2000, he said, he hoped to reverse Japan’s severe demographic decline. 首席执行官石坂茂表示，他认为IBJ的使命不仅仅是为了赚钱。他说，当他在2000年离开银行业并进入婚介行业时，他希望能扭转日本严重的人口下降趋势。 “Since Japanese society rarely conceives children outside of wedlock, I realized a matching service specifically focused on marriage would have a vital future,” he said. “由于日本社会很少在婚外生育，我意识到，专门针对婚姻的匹配服务将拥有至关重要的未来，”他说。 Recently, that mission got a dose of encouraging news. In the first six months of 2026, births in Japan rose 0.8 percent, the first increase in 11 years for that period, according to the Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare. The modest uptick followed two straight years of increased marriages. 最近，这一使命迎来了一个令人鼓舞的好消息。据日本厚生劳动省的数据，2026年前六个月里，日本的出生人数增长了0.8%，这是11年来该时期内首次出现增长。在这一温和回升之前，日本的结婚人数已连续两年实现增长。 Mr. Yasuda, the IBJ client, said he hoped to contribute to those numbers. Part of his desire to marry quickly, he said, comes from wanting to start early enough to raise three or four children. IBJ客户安田泰然表示，他希望能为这些数字做出贡献。他说，他渴望尽快结婚，部分原因是想尽早开始生育，以便有时间养育三四个孩子。 Mr. Ishizaka sees clients like Mr. Yasuda as evidence that a generation frequently portrayed as retreating from marriage may instead be looking for a more efficient route toward it. 石坂茂将像安田泰然这样的客户视为一种证明，这一代人虽然常被描绘为对婚姻退缩，但实际上，他们可能正在寻找一条更高效的通往婚姻之路。 “Surveys consistently show that over 80 percent of young people say they want to marry if they find the right partner,” he said. “I am certain that every married couple we create contributes directly to reversing the birthrate decline.” “调查始终显示，超过80%的年轻人表示，如果找到合适的伴侣，他们是想结婚的，”他说。“我确信，我们撮合的每一对已婚夫妇都在为扭转出生率下降做出直接贡献。” River Akira Davis常驻东京，报道日本经济和商业新闻。 Kiuko Notoya是一名常驻东京的记者/研究员，报道日本新闻。 翻译：晋其角 点击查看本文英文版。 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site

But in Japan, 20-somethings are flocking to marriage agencies that promise a fast track to the altar — and charge a premium for it. 真爱可能是无价的。但在日本，二十多岁的年轻人正涌向婚姻介绍所，这些机构承诺提供通往婚姻殿堂的捷径，并为此收取高额费用。 For hundreds of years, through the post-World War II era, Japanese marriages were brokered through “omiai,” a practice in which matchmakers — usually relatives, family friends or bosses — linked singles in their orbit. But the custom fell out of fashion, giving way to organic dating and, eventually, a wave of casual-dating apps. 直至二战后时期，数百年来日本的婚姻都是通过“相亲”来撮合的，根据这种习俗，媒人——通常是亲戚、世交或老板——为身边的单身人士牵线搭桥。但这种习俗后来不再流行，取而代之的是顺其自然的约会，最终被休闲约会应用的浪潮取代。 Now, young adults are enrolling at record rates in marriage agencies, where counselors serve as professional matchmakers. Across Tokyo, advertisements line metro cars, urging commuters to “leave life’s fateful encounters to the pros.” Another declares: “Better one omiai than 100 swipes.” 如今，年轻人正以创纪录的比例在婚姻介绍所注册，那里的顾问担任着专业媒人的角色。在整个东京，地铁车厢里布满了广告，敦促通勤者“把人生中注定的相遇交给专业人士”。另一则广告宣称：“一次相亲胜过滑动屏幕一百次。” Experts say the shift is being driven by a backlash against frustrations familiar to modern daters globally. With social circles shrinking, young Japanese — tired of the ghosting, catfishing and noncommittal matches rampant on dating apps — are turning to hands-on human guidance for greater efficiency and assurance. 专家表示，种转变源于全球现代约会者对常见挫折感的一种反噬。随着社交圈的缩小，日本年轻人厌倦了在约会应用上泛滥的“玩失踪”、网络身份造假和不愿承诺的配对——正转向需要亲力亲为的人工指导，以获得更高的效率和保障。 Among the new recruits was Taizen Yasuda. A soft-spoken 28-year-old, he said he had run out of patience for algorithm-driven romance. 安田泰然（音）就是这些新注册者中的一员。这位说话轻声细语的28岁年轻人表示，他对算法驱动的恋爱已经失去了耐心。 “The process of endless matching, messaging and finally meeting on apps was exhausting,” Mr. Yasuda said. Matchmaking services, he thought, “would be the quickest way to find someone with the exact same goal — marriage.” “在交友软件上无休止地匹配、发信息，最后见面，这个过程令人筋疲力尽，”安田泰然说。他认为，相亲服务“将是找到有着结婚这个相同目标者的最快方式”。 The practice is resurging as Japan grapples with a shrinking population and fewer young families. Because childbearing in Japan remains overwhelmingly tied to marriage, encouraging more people to wed has become part of the country’s broader push to boost its birthrate. 随着日本努力应对 人口萎缩 和年轻家庭减少的问题，这种做法正在复苏。由于在日本，生育仍然绝大程度上与婚姻挂钩，因此鼓励更多人结婚已成为该国提高出生率的更广泛举措的一部分。 28岁的安田泰然与他的IBJ顾问在一起。他表示，他很感谢通过顾问转达的约会对象的反馈意见。 Noriko Hayashi for The New York Times One company has positioned itself at the center of the matchmaking trend: IBJ, a Tokyo-based giant with a nationwide network. Promising to take clients from first meeting to proposal in three months, the company has seen membership and profits soar. It now claims a hand in roughly one of every 25 marriages in Japan. 一家公司将自己定位在这一相亲趋势的中心：总部位于东京、拥有全国性网络的巨头IBJ。这家公司承诺在三个月内让客户从初次见面走向求婚，其会员数量和利润都在飙升。该公司目前声称，日本大约每25场婚姻中就有一场是他们撮合的。 Mr. Yasuda is part of a wave of young singles who have joined IBJ. On a recent Sunday, he sat across from his counselor in a quiet consultation room, clad in a stiffly pressed suit, with a sweep of wavy hair combed to the side. A little over a month after joining the matchmaking service, Mr. Yasuda had already narrowed his prospects to two women. He had just taken one on a weekend drive to see a field of yellow canola blooms. 安田泰然是加入IBJ的年轻单身人士中的一员。在最近的一个周日，他坐在安静的咨询室里，坐在顾问的对面，穿着笔挺的西装，梳着偏分的卷发。在加入这项相亲服务一个多月后，安田泰然已经将潜在对象缩小到两名女性。他刚刚带了其中一位在周末自驾出游，欣赏一片盛开的黄色油菜花田。 Every member is assigned a consultant who micromanages the courtship process. The consultants advise on everything from grooming and messaging etiquette to date itineraries. 每位会员都会被分配一位顾问，负责细致管理整个求偶过程。顾问会就各方面提供建议，从仪容打扮、发信息礼仪到约会行程。 When two members match, their consultants work in tandem behind the scenes, doing what they call “Cupid work” — exchanging and filtering postdate feedback and helping orchestrate every milestone, down to an eventual proposal. 当两名成员匹配成功时，他们的顾问会在幕后协同工作，做他们所说的“丘比特工作”——交流和筛选约会后的反馈，协助安排每一个重要节点，直至最终的求婚。 “We are providing the kind of support only humans can offer to help people get married as quickly as possible,” said Shigeru Ishizaka, IBJ’s chief executive. “我们提供只有人类才能提供的那种支持，帮助人们尽快结婚，”IBJ首席执行官石坂茂表示。 IBJ的顾问畑惠子就方方面面提供建议，从仪容仪表、短信礼仪到约会行程安排。 In an increasingly digitized society, “there is a deep desire to have a person guiding you through the process of dating,” said Junko Yamada, a lecturer at Tokai University in Tokyo who studies the psychology of romance. Echoing the reassurance of traditional omiai, she said having an expert curate matches offered psychological safety. 在一个日益数字化的社会中，“人们内心深处渴望有人能在约会过程中提供指导，”在东京东海大学研究恋爱心理学的讲师山田顺子说。她表示，与传统相亲带来的安心感相应，由专家来精心挑选匹配对象能提供心理安全感。 Ms. Yamada said that today’s youths seemed fixated on maximizing efficiency in every aspect of their lives, and that these agencies appealed to that mind-set by filtering out people who weren’t serious about marriage. 山田顺子说，如今的年轻人似乎追求在生活的方方面面实现效率最大化，而这些机构通过过滤掉那些对婚姻不认真的对象，迎合了这种心态。 IBJ’s network of affiliated marriage agencies has varying costs and eligibility rules. Members typically pay about $30 to $100 a month, an enrollment fee of $650 to $1,300 and an additional $1,300 “success fee” if a couple get engaged. It also charges a $1,300 fee if couples violate its rules against “banned activities,” including premarital sex and cohabitation. IBJ said its counselors tracked the progression of their clients’ relationships. IBJ附属婚姻介绍所网络有着不同的收费标准和资格规定。会员通常每月支付约30至100美元，注册费为650至1300美元，如果两人订婚，还需额外支付1300美元的“成功费”。如果情侣违反该机构关于“禁止活动”（包括婚前性行为和同居）的规定，该机构还会收取1300美元的罚金。IBJ表示，其顾问会跟踪客户关系的发展。 Enrollment is generally limited to applicants with steady incomes. IBJ’s largest directly operated agency accepts only women ages 20 to 39 and men ages 25 to 49. 注册通常仅限于有稳定收入的申请人。IBJ最大的直营机构只接受20至39岁的女性和25至49岁的男性。 Critics argue that corporate services like IBJ, a company listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange with annual revenue exceeding $130 million, strip the soul from traditional matchmaking, impose rigid timelines on anxious young adults and turn dating into a moneymaking endeavor. 批评人士认为，像IBJ这样的企业化婚介服务剥夺了传统相亲的灵魂，给焦虑的年轻人强加了死板的时间表，将约会变成了一项赚钱的生意。IBJ已在东京证券交易所上市，年收入超过1.3亿美元。 “现代婚介机构做不到我做的事，”东京附近的一位资深婚介人加藤郁子说。 Among the skeptics is Ikuko Kato, a veteran matchmaker who operates from her lace-curtained home just outside Tokyo, filled with hundreds of smiling pictures of couples she has matched. Dressed in pearls and a pink knit suit, Ms. Kato said she had matched more than 1,300 couples over 44 years and claimed that not a single pair had divorced. 加藤郁子（音）就是这些怀疑者之一。这位资深媒人经营着一家家庭式婚介所，它位于东京郊外、挂着蕾丝窗帘，里面摆满了数百张她撮合的情侣的照片，每个人都笑容满面。加藤郁子戴着珍珠项链，穿着粉色针织套装，她说自己在44年里撮合了1300多对情侣，而且没有一对离婚。 “They’re too focused on business,” said Ms. Kato, who also charges clients a monthly fee as well as a fee if her matchmaking results in marriage. “My parents were neighborhood matchmakers. It’s in my blood. Modern corporate agents cannot do what I do.” “它们太注重商业了，”加藤郁子说，她也向客户收取月费，如果相亲成功结婚也会收取一笔费用。“我的父母就是街坊邻里间的媒人。这融入了我的血液。现代的企业婚介机构做不了我做的事情。” Unlike neighborhood matchmakers, IBJ moves clients through a lucrative, end-to-end program. Beyond matchmaking, its group companies offer wedding planning, financial consulting and housing services, along with referrals to affiliated businesses like eyebrow-grooming salons. 与邻里间的媒人不一样，IBJ为客户提供一条高利润的端到端服务流程。除了相亲，其集团公司还提供婚礼策划、财务咨询和住房服务，还会将客户推荐给修眉沙龙等合作商家。 Membership has grown about 50 percent over the past five years, and IBJ reported a 44 percent jump in first-half revenue this year, to about $91 million. 过去五年里，其会员人数增长了约50%，IBJ报告称，今年上半年的收入激增了44%，达到约9100万美元。 加藤郁子的家中挂满了她牵线搭桥的1300多对情侣的照片。她声称，这些情侣中没有一对离婚。 Mr. Ishizaka, the chief executive, said he viewed IBJ’s mission as more than just money. When he left banking and entered the matchmaking industry in 2000, he said, he hoped to reverse Japan’s severe demographic decline. 首席执行官石坂茂表示，他认为IBJ的使命不仅仅是为了赚钱。他说，当他在2000年离开银行业并进入婚介行业时，他希望能扭转日本严重的人口下降趋势。 “Since Japanese society rarely conceives children outside of wedlock, I realized a matching service specifically focused on marriage would have a vital future,” he said. “由于日本社会很少在婚外生育，我意识到，专门针对婚姻的匹配服务将拥有至关重要的未来，”他说。 Recently, that mission got a dose of encouraging news. In the first six months of 2026, births in Japan rose 0.8 percent, the first increase in 11 years for that period, according to the Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare. The modest uptick followed two straight years of increased marriages. 最近，这一使命迎来了一个令人鼓舞的好消息。据日本厚生劳动省的数据，2026年前六个月里，日本的出生人数增长了0.8%，这是11年来该时期内首次出现增长。在这一温和回升之前，日本的结婚人数已连续两年实现增长。 Mr. Yasuda, the IBJ client, said he hoped to contribute to those numbers. Part of his desire to marry quickly, he said, comes from wanting to start early enough to raise three or four children. IBJ客户安田泰然表示，他希望能为这些数字做出贡献。他说，他渴望尽快结婚，部分原因是想尽早开始生育，以便有时间养育三四个孩子。 Mr. Ishizaka sees clients like Mr. Yasuda as evidence that a generation frequently portrayed as retreating from marriage may instead be looking for a more efficient route toward it. 石坂茂将像安田泰然这样的客户视为一种证明，这一代人虽然常被描绘为对婚姻退缩，但实际上，他们可能正在寻找一条更高效的通往婚姻之路。 “Surveys consistently show that over 80 percent of young people say they want to marry if they find the right partner,” he said. “I am certain that every married couple we create contributes directly to reversing the birthrate decline.” “调查始终显示，超过80%的年轻人表示，如果找到合适的伴侣，他们是想结婚的，”他说。“我确信，我们撮合的每一对已婚夫妇都在为扭转出生率下降做出直接贡献。” River Akira Davis 常驻东京，报道日本经济和商业新闻。 Kiuko Notoya 是一名常驻东京的记者/研究员，报道日本新闻。 翻译：晋其角 点击查看本文英文版。 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site

title: 特朗普令美国面临三重病毒威胁
description: 托马斯·弗里德曼2026年9月30日 Ioulex for The New York Times President Trump is such an awful human being that just writing about him feels degrading. What president would denigrate his predecessor in front of China’s leader the way Trump mocked Joe Biden, now suffering from cancer, by pointing out that a framed picture of an autopen was hanging in the White House instead of Biden’s portrait? 特朗普总统是个烂人，光是写他都让人觉得掉价。有哪位总统会像特朗普那样，在中国领导人面前贬损自己的前任——他拿如今身患癌症的乔·拜登开涮，特意指出白宫里原本该挂拜登肖像的地方，现在挂的却是一幅自动签名笔的照片。 Alas, though, when someone as morally warped as Trump — whose first secretary of state called him a “moron” — assumes this much unchecked power at the dawn of the Age of Artificial Intelligence, he can’t be ignored. Because right now Trump is leaving America exposed to dangerous viruses: digital, biological and diplomatic. Something bad is going to happen to us as a result. We and our children are going to pay for this, and not only at the gas pump. 唉，可是，当像特朗普这样道德扭曲的人——他的第一任国务卿曾称他为“白痴”——在人工智能时代来临之际掌握如此不受制约的权力时，我们就不能对他视而不见。因为眼下特朗普正让美国暴露在危险的病毒之下：数字病毒、生物病毒和外交病毒。结果一定会有坏事发生在我们身上。我们和我们的后代都将为此付出代价，而且代价绝不只体现在更高的油价上。 Let me start with the digital virus now on the loose. Recently, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Google all disclosed incidents in which their artificial intelligence models escaped their controls and gallivanted about hacking other computer systems — including an Australian government website, the Hugging Face platform and websites of the U.S. Commerce Department and the Securities and Exchange Commission. Remember, these are infant A.I. systems; they’re still in diapers and yet to be supercharged by fully training themselves and leaving their human designers behind. 让我先从正在失控的数字病毒说起。最近，OpenAI、Anthropic、Meta和谷歌都披露了各自人工智能模型脱离控制、四处入侵其他计算机系统的事件——包括一个澳大利亚政府网站、Hugging Face平台，以及美国商务部和证券交易委员会的网站。别忘了，这些还只是处于婴儿期的人工智能系统；它们还在穿尿布，尚未通过完全自主训练、摆脱人类设计者而变得无比强大。 And remember, too, the stories above are about what the good guys are doing. Talk to any major cyberprotection expert at any major U.S. company, and you’ll be terrified by stories about what the bad guys are doing with smaller A.I. models that they have gotten their hands on, with the controls stripped out. 也别忘了，上面这些还只是“好人”在做的事。随便找一家美国大公司里的任何一位资深网络安全专聊聊，你都会被“坏人”用他们弄到手、已经去掉安全限制的小型人工智能模型所做的事吓坏。 The CrowdStrike Global Threat Report said attacks by “A.I.-enabled adversaries” increased by 89 percent in 2025 compared with the previous year, Infosecurity Magazine reported in February — and the rate has soared since. 网络安全公司CrowdStrike的《全球威胁报告》称，与上一年相比，2025年由“人工智能赋能的对手”发起的攻击增加了89%，《信息安全杂志》今年2月报道了这一数据——而此后这一速度还在飙升。 But fear not, because our president, who doesn’t even use email, told the United Nations last week that he knows that our fears about A.I. safety are fraudulent. He referred to “the very same people who said we’ll all be dead in 12 years because of global warming.” He added: “And nobody was dead. These are the same people that are now saying that A.I. is going to kill us all.” (Untold thousands have died in catastrophes worsened by climate change in the last decade, and only in Trump’s fetid imagination did anyone say, “Sir, we’ll all be dead in 12 years.”) 不过别害怕，因为我们这位连电子邮件都不用的总统上周在联合国告诉我们，他知道我们对人工智能安全的担忧是骗局。他提到“正是那些说我们都会在12年内因为全球变暖而死掉的人”。他还说：“结果没人死。现在又是同一批人在说人工智能会把我们全杀死。”（过去十年里，已有成千上万的人死于因气候变化而加剧的灾难，而只有在特朗普肮脏的想象里，才有人说：“先生，我们都会在12年内死掉。”） Trump and his party — and the A.I. tech bros who have effectively paid them to keep their hands off their industry — had better pray that the “October surprise” in this coming midterm election is not a major, destructive A.I. event. If it is, they’d better have their spaceships ready to whisk them off to another planet where they can live forever, because this one may make their existences a living hell. 特朗普和他的政党——连同那些实际上等于花钱买通他们、让政府对AI产业撒手不管的科技哥们——最好祈祷，在即将到来的这场中期选举中，那个所谓的“10月惊奇”不会是一场重大的、具有破坏性的人工智能事件。如果真是，他们最好提前备好飞船，把自己送到另一个能获得永生的星球上去，因为这个世界可能会让他们活得生不如死。 This A.I. threat is not a hoax (nor is the climate threat a hoax, as Trump would know if he ever looked at his own administration’s NASA website). The only hoax is that Trump, who once suggested injecting bleach might be a good way to rid yourself of Covid-19, thinks he knows anything about A.I. or climate change — or bleach. 人工智能威胁不是骗局（气候威胁也不是骗局，只要特朗普哪怕看一眼他自己政府的NASA网站就会知道）。唯一的骗局是：特朗普——他曾建议注射漂白剂或许是摆脱新冠病毒的好办法——竟然认为自己懂人工智能、气候变化，或者漂白剂。 “It’s not a hoax at all,” Bill Gates said in an interview on NBC’s “Meet the Press” on Sunday. Gates said that the United States should restrain A.I. development until tougher safeguards are in place, and he argued that China would most likely do the same if Washington took the initiative to draft new rules to regulate the use of A.I. “这根本不是什么骗局，”比尔·盖茨周日在美国全国广播公司的《与媒体见面》节目中接受采访时说。盖茨表示，在建立更严格的安全保障措施之前，美国应该限制人工智能的发展；他还认为，如果华盛顿率先起草新规则，对人工智能的使用加以规范，中国很可能也会跟进。 A.I. without proper regulation is “completely irresponsible,” Gates said. “You need law enforcement and the politicians to get into the discussion about what safeguards and monitoring look like.” He concluded: “A.I. is certainly powerful enough to drive events that, you know, cause a billion deaths.” 盖茨说，在缺乏适当监管的情况下发展人工智能是“完全不负责任的”。“执法部门和政界人士必须参与进来，讨论应该建立怎样的安全保障和监督机制。”最后他说：“人工智能的力量肯定足以引发那种，你知道，造成十亿人死亡的事件。” Precisely because there has never been such a tool, despite its destructive potential, with so much promise to solve so many energy, climate and medical problems for humanity, I want to see A.I. thrive, as does Gates. Which is why we should all want to prevent now an A.I.-driven Sept. 11 that would completely delegitimize artificial intelligence in the public eye. That would be a double tragedy. 正因为从未有过这样一种工具——尽管它一方面具有巨大的破坏潜力，另一方面又有望帮助人类解决如此之多的能源、气候和医疗问题——所以和盖茨一样，我也希望看到人工智能蓬勃发展。也正因如此，我们现在就应该设法避免发生一场由人工智能引发的“9·11”式灾难，因为那会让人工智能在公众眼中彻底失去正当性。那将是一场双重悲剧。 I wish that the only threat to us from Trump’s unrestrained ignorance were an A.I. virus. Sadly, last week, my Times colleague Apoorva Mandavilli reported that America’s Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, long the “undisputed global leader in public health,” has been so systematically dismantled by Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. that it is now “a skeleton of the powerhouse it was.” 我希望特朗普那种不受约束的无知给我们带来的唯一威胁只是人工智能病毒。遗憾的是，上周我的时报同事阿普尔瓦·曼达维利报道说，美国疾病控制和预防中心——长期以来是“公共卫生领域无可争议的全球领导者”——在卫生部长小罗伯特·肯尼迪系统性的拆解之下，如今只剩下“一副空架子，早已不复当年之强盛”。 Not only has the C.D.C.’s staff been reduced by some 30 percent, but, Mandavilli reported, citing current and former employees, “the changes have hindered the C.D.C.’s ability to respond to outbreaks as measles spreads at home and Ebola abroad, and to issue timely guidance on vaccinations as cooling temperatures kick off the respiratory season. … Entire divisions have been shuttered, including teams that worked on smoking, sexual violence, child abuse and falls among older adults.” 曼达维利援引现任和前任员工的话报道，疾控中心不仅人员减少了约30%，而且“这些变化削弱了疾控中心在国内麻疹蔓延、国外埃博拉疫情之际应对疫情暴发的能力，也削弱了其在气温下降、呼吸道疾病季开始之际及时发布疫苗接种指引的能力……一些部门被一锅端，包括负责吸烟、性暴力、虐待儿童和老年人跌倒问题的团队”。 The Guardian newspaper carried a story about the spreading outbreak of measles in Pennsylvania, which has now topped 900 cases. Dr. John Goldman, an infectious disease specialist at the University of Pittsburgh Medical Center, said that between 1992 and 2026, he hadn’t seen a single case, The Guardian reported. Now, “We’re seeing at least one every day,” and he added, “Never in my life did I think I was ever going to see measles again.” This is an example of how Trump’s negligence is helping to spread actual, biological viruses. 《卫报》刊登了一篇关于宾夕法尼亚州麻疹疫情蔓延的报道，目前当地病例数已超过900例。报道援引匹兹堡大学医学中心传染病专家约翰·戈德曼博士的话说，从1992年到2026年，他一个病例都没有见过。可现在，“我们每天至少能见到一例”。他还说：“我这辈子从没想过自己还会再次看到麻疹。”这正是特朗普的失职如何助长真正的、生物意义上的病毒传播的一个例子。 But don’t forget the anti-diplomatic virus also sapping our strength. What is that? Check out this story in the Israeli newspaper Haaretz, by its Middle East affairs expert Zvi Bar’el. It was about how the diplomatic incompetence of the Trump administration and the malevolence of the cabinet of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have combined to grind the 20-point Trump peace plan for Gaza to a halt. So Gazan civilians, many living in war-broken buildings, one of which collapsed on Sept. 16, killing at least 21 people, including 11 children, remain in total squalor. 但也别忘了那股同样在削弱我们实力的反外交病毒。那是什么？看看以色列《国土报》上中东事务专家兹维·巴雷尔写的这篇报道。它讲的是特朗普政府的外交无能和本雅明·内塔尼亚胡内阁的恶意是如何结合起来，使特朗普那份20点加沙和平计划陷入停滞。于是，加沙平民——许多人住在被战争摧毁的建筑物里，其中一栋于9月16日倒塌，造成至少21人死亡，包括11名儿童——仍生活在彻底的悲惨境地中。 When Trump launched his vaunted Gaza Board of Peace and made himself chairman, participating countries pledged $17 billion for Gaza. But “as far as is known, less than $300 million has been transferred,” Bar’el reported. 当特朗普启动他吹嘘的加沙和平委员会并亲自担任主席时，参与国承诺为加沙提供170亿美元。但据巴雷尔报道，“目前已知到账的钱不到3亿美元。” Moreover, the peace plan’s international stabilization force has yet to be established. The Palestinian police force to replace Hamas, which is supposed to operate under a Palestinian technocratic government, was supposed to receive training in Egypt, “but Israel is preventing them from leaving Gaza,” according to Bar’el. 此外，和平计划的国际维和部队尚未建立。原本应在巴勒斯坦技术官僚政府下运作、取代哈马斯的巴勒斯坦警察部队本应在埃及接受训练，“但以色列阻止他们离开加沙，”巴雷尔说。 Then Bar’el peeled back the real story: “The stalemate in Gaza serves Israel. Hamas no longer poses a security threat, but as long as it holds territory, Israel retains a pretext for resuming the war. And as long as the Strip remains devastated and unlivable, the pressure on the people to leave only grows.” He added that Netanyahu’s defense minister, Israel Katz, after being criticized by a rival politician for not achieving a more decisive victory over Hamas, declared that the Israeli military was ready, if ordered, to eliminate Hamas “so that the emigration plan can be implemented.” 随后巴雷尔揭开了真正的故事：“加沙的僵局有利于以色列。哈马斯不再构成安全威胁，但只要它控制着领土，以色列就保留着恢复战争的借口。而只要加沙地带仍被毁坏、无法居住，民众离开的压力就只会增大。”他还说，在一名政敌批评未能对哈马斯取得更决定性胜利后，内塔尼亚胡的国防部长以色列·卡茨宣称，只要一声令下，以色列军方随时可以消灭哈马斯，“以便移民计划得以实施。” So that the emigration plan can be implemented. 以便移民计划得以实施。 Really? What is that? That is Orwellian speak for the ethnic cleansing of Gaza of Palestinians by the Netanyahu government. And what have Trump and his secretary of state, Marco Rubio, said in response? Zilch. 真的？那是什么？是内塔尼亚胡政府对加沙巴勒斯坦人进行种族清洗的奥威尔式说法。而特朗普和他的国务卿马可·鲁比奥对此作何回应？什么都没有。 I’ve learned over the years that diplomacy operates like a virus as well, beneficially or detrimentally: The more success you have, the more respect you get; the more respect you get, the more success you have. Conversely, the more failure you have, the less allies trust joining you, so the more failure you have. 这些年来我学到，外交也像病毒一样运作，不管是有益或有害：你越成功，得到的尊重越多；得到的尊重越多，你就越成功。反过来，越失败，盟友就越不愿加入你，于是你就越失败。 Example: Between March and October 1991, Secretary of State James A. Baker III made eight diplomatic trips to the Middle East to put together the Madrid peace conference — the first among Israel, the Palestine Liberation Organization and several Arab states. I made all eight trips with him as The Times’s diplomatic correspondent. He failed on the first seven, but Baker would not quit and he got it done on the eighth. 比如1991年3月至10月间，国务卿詹姆斯·A·贝克三世八次出访中东，促成马德里和会——这是以色列、巴勒斯坦解放组织和几个阿拉伯国家之间的首次和会。我作为时报外交记者随他八次出访。前七次他都失败了，但贝克没有放弃，第八次成功了。 Show me a single diplomatic initiative the Trump administration has built since the cease-fire in Gaza, which Trump has left to languish. It’s as if all he cared about was the headline from the signing, after which he amazingly declared last Oct. 13: “Together, we’ve achieved what everybody said was impossible. At long last we have peace in the Middle East.” 特朗普政府在加沙停火后促成了哪怕一项外交倡议吗？特朗普任由加沙在一片废墟之中。就好像他只在乎签字时的新闻报道，之后竟在去年10月13日宣称：“我们共同实现了所有人都说不可能的事。中东终于有了和平。” Now that’s what I call a real hoax. 这才是我所说的真正骗局。 There is no energetic, focused follow-up because there are no clear lines of authority. You have Thomas Barrack, who is the special envoy for Syria and Iraq and the ambassador to Turkey, making his own policy statements. You have Massad Fares Boulos, the father-in-law of Trump’s daughter Tiffany, serving as a senior adviser to the president of the United States on Arab and Middle Eastern affairs. You have part-timers, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff. You have various assistant secretaries of state and defense. And you have Trump on his social media feed. (Somebody is going to make this into a musical!) 没有有力、专注的后续行动，是因为没有明确的权力链条。我们看到托马斯·巴拉克（叙利亚和伊拉克问题特使兼驻土耳其大使）自己在发表政策声明。看到马萨德·法雷斯·布洛斯（特朗普女儿蒂芙尼的公公）在担任美国总统的阿拉伯和中东事务高级顾问。看到兼职的贾里德·库什纳和史蒂夫·维特科夫。看到各种助理国务卿和助理国防部长。还有特朗普的社交媒体动态。（这些将来会被人写成一出音乐剧的！） What you don’t have is a secretary of state like Baker, relentlessly focusing and leveraging American power and making trip after trip after trip until he gets the job done. 我们没有看到的是，像贝克那样的国务卿，死咬着不放，并利用美国的力量，一次又一次出访，直到把事情办成。 The only thing Trump relentlessly follows up on is harassing the press. Last Saturday, after being forced by a judge to allow CNN reporters back in the White House after Trump illegally banned them because their coverage was not fawning enough, the president nevertheless blocked CNN from accompanying him on Air Force One to attend a football game in Tennessee. 而特朗普死咬着不放的是媒体。上周六，在一名法官迫使白宫允许CNN记者重返白宫之后——此前特朗普因他们的报道不够谄媚而非法禁止他们进入——总统还是禁止CNN随他乘坐空军一号前往田纳西州观看一场橄榄球赛。 When it comes to denouncing the press, Trump is laser-focused. But when dealing with the digital, biological and diplomatic viruses weakening our national immune system, not so much — to our great peril. 在谴责媒体方面，特朗普的注意力是高度集中的。但在应对削弱我们国家免疫系统的数字、生物和外交病毒时，就没那么专注了——而这将给我们带来巨大危险。 托马斯·L·弗里德曼(Thomas L. Friedman)是外交事务方面的专栏作者。他1981年加入时报，曾三次获得普利策奖。他著有七本书，包括赢得国家图书奖的《从贝鲁特到耶路撒冷》(From Beirut to Jerusalem)。欢迎在X和Facebook上关注他。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。
content: 托马斯·弗里德曼 2026年9月30日 Ioulex for The New York Times President Trump is such an awful human being that just writing about him feels degrading. What president would denigrate his predecessor in front of China’s leader the way Trump mocked Joe Biden , now suffering from cancer, by pointing out that a framed picture of an autopen was hanging in the White House instead of Biden’s portrait? 特朗普总统是个烂人，光是写他都让人觉得掉价。有哪位总统会像特朗普那样，在中国领导人面前贬损自己的前任——他拿如今身患癌症的乔·拜登 开涮 ，特意指出白宫里原本该挂拜登肖像的地方，现在挂的却是一幅自动签名笔的照片。 Alas, though, when someone as morally warped as Trump — whose first secretary of state called him a “moron ” — assumes this much unchecked power at the dawn of the Age of Artificial Intelligence, he can’t be ignored. Because right now Trump is leaving America exposed to dangerous viruses: digital, biological and diplomatic. Something bad is going to happen to us as a result. We and our children are going to pay for this, and not only at the gas pump. 唉，可是，当像特朗普这样道德扭曲的人——他的第一任国务卿曾称他为“ 白痴 ”——在人工智能时代来临之际掌握如此不受制约的权力时，我们就不能对他视而不见。因为眼下特朗普正让美国暴露在危险的病毒之下：数字病毒、生物病毒和外交病毒。结果一定会有坏事发生在我们身上。我们和我们的后代都将为此付出代价，而且代价绝不只体现在更高的油价上。 Let me start with the digital virus now on the loose. Recently, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Google all disclosed incidents in which their artificial intelligence models escaped their controls and gallivanted about hacking other computer systems — including an Australian government website, the Hugging Face platform and websites of the U.S. Commerce Department and the Securities and Exchange Commission. Remember, these are infant A.I. systems; they’re still in diapers and yet to be supercharged by fully training themselves and leaving their human designers behind. 让我先从正在失控的数字病毒说起。最近，OpenAI、Anthropic、Meta和谷歌 都 披露 了各自人工智能模型脱离控制、四处入侵其他计算机系统的 事件 ——包括一个澳大利亚政府网站、Hugging Face平台，以及美国商务部和证券交易委员会的 网站 。别忘了，这些还只是处于婴儿期的人工智能系统；它们还在穿尿布，尚未通过完全自主训练、摆脱人类设计者而变得无比强大。 And remember, too, the stories above are about what the good guys are doing. Talk to any major cyberprotection expert at any major U.S. company, and you’ll be terrified by stories about what the bad guys are doing with smaller A.I. models that they have gotten their hands on, with the controls stripped out. 也别忘了，上面这些还只是“好人”在做的事。随便找一家美国大公司里的任何一位资深网络安全专聊聊，你都会被“坏人”用他们弄到手、已经去掉安全限制的小型人工智能模型所做的事吓坏。 The CrowdStrike Global Threat Report said attacks by “A.I.-enabled adversaries” increased by 89 percent in 2025 compared with the previous year, Infosecurity Magazine reported in February — and the rate has soared since. 网络安全公司CrowdStrike的《全球威胁报告》称，与上一年相比，2025年由“人工智能赋能的对手”发起的攻击增加了89%， 《信息安全杂志》 今年2月报道了这一数据——而此后这一速度还在 飙升 。 But fear not, because our president, who doesn’t even use email, told the United Nations last week that he knows that our fears about A.I. safety are fraudulent. He referred to “the very same people who said we’ll all be dead in 12 years because of global warming.” He added: “And nobody was dead. These are the same people that are now saying that A.I. is going to kill us all.” ( Untold thousands have died in catastrophes worsened by climate change in the last decade, and only in Trump’s fetid imagination did anyone say, “Sir, we’ll all be dead in 12 years.”) 不过别害怕，因为我们这位连电子邮件都不用的总统上周在联合国告诉我们，他知道我们对人工智能安全的担忧是骗局。他提到“正是那些说我们都会在12年内因为全球变暖而死掉的人”。他还说：“结果没人死。现在又是同一批人在说人工智能会把我们全杀死。”（过去十年里，已有 成千上万的人死于 因气候变化而加剧的灾难，而只有在特朗普肮脏的想象里，才有人说：“先生，我们都会在12年内死掉。”） Trump and his party — and the A.I. tech bros who have effectively paid them to keep their hands off their industry — had better pray that the “October surprise” in this coming midterm election is not a major, destructive A.I. event. If it is, they’d better have their spaceships ready to whisk them off to another planet where they can live forever, because this one may make their existences a living hell. 特朗普和他的政党——连同那些实际上等于花钱 买通 他们、让政府对AI产业撒手不管的科技哥们——最好祈祷，在即将到来的这场中期选举中，那个所谓的“10月惊奇”不会是一场重大的、具有破坏性的人工智能事件。如果真是，他们最好提前备好飞船，把自己送到另一个能获得永生的星球上去，因为这个世界可能会让他们活得生不如死。 This A.I. threat is not a hoax (nor is the climate threat a hoax, as Trump would know if he ever looked at his own administration’s NASA website ). Gates said that the United States should restrain A.I. development until tougher safeguards are in place, and he argued that China would most likely do the same if Washington took the initiative to draft new rules to regulate the use of A.I. “这根本不是什么骗局，”比尔·盖茨周日在美国全国广播公司的《与媒体见面》节目中接受采访时说。盖茨表示，在建立更严格的安全保障措施之前，美国应该限制人工智能的发展；他还认为，如果华盛顿率先起草新规则，对人工智能的使用加以规范，中国很可能也会跟进。 A.I. without proper regulation is “completely irresponsible,” Gates said. “You need law enforcement and the politicians to get into the discussion about what safeguards and monitoring look like.” He concluded: “A.I. is certainly powerful enough to drive events that, you know, cause a billion deaths.” 盖茨说，在缺乏适当监管的情况下发展人工智能是“完全不负责任的”。“执法部门和政界人士必须参与进来，讨论应该建立怎样的安全保障和监督机制。”最后他说：“人工智能的力量肯定足以引发那种，你知道，造成十亿人死亡的事件。” Precisely because there has never been such a tool, despite its destructive potential, with so much promise to solve so many energy, climate and medical problems for humanity, I want to see A.I. thrive, as does Gates. Which is why we should all want to prevent now an A.I.-driven Sept. 11 that would completely delegitimize artificial intelligence in the public eye. What is that? Check out this story in the Israeli newspaper Haaretz , by its Middle East affairs expert Zvi Bar’el. It was about how the diplomatic incompetence of the Trump administration and the malevolence of the cabinet of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have combined to grind the 20-point Trump peace plan for Gaza to a halt. So Gazan civilians, many living in war-broken buildings, one of which collapsed on Sept. 16, killing at least 21 people, including 11 children, remain in total squalor. 但也别忘了那股同样在削弱我们实力的反外交病毒。那是什么？看看以色列 《国土报》 上中东事务专家兹维·巴雷尔写的这篇报道。它讲的是特朗普政府的外交无能和本雅明·内塔尼亚胡内阁的恶意是如何结合起来，使特朗普那份20点加沙和平计划陷入停滞。于是，加沙平民——许多人住在被战争摧毁的建筑物里，其中一栋于9月16日倒塌， 造成至少21人死亡，包括11名儿童 ——仍生活在彻底的悲惨境地中。 When Trump launched his vaunted Gaza Board of Peace and made himself chairman, participating countries pledged $17 billion for Gaza. But “as far as is known, less than $300 million has been transferred,” Bar’el reported. 当特朗普启动他吹嘘的加沙和平委员会并亲自担任主席时，参与国承诺为加沙提供170亿美元。但据巴雷尔报道，“目前已知到账的钱不到3亿美元。” Moreover, the peace plan’s international stabilization force has yet to be established. The Palestinian police force to replace Hamas, which is supposed to operate under a Palestinian technocratic government, was supposed to receive training in Egypt, “but Israel is preventing them from leaving Gaza,” according to Bar’el. 此外，和平计划的国际维和部队尚未建立。原本应在巴勒斯坦技术官僚政府下运作、取代哈马斯的巴勒斯坦警察部队本应在埃及接受训练，“但以色列阻止他们离开加沙，”巴雷尔说。 Then Bar’el peeled back the real story: “The stalemate in Gaza serves Israel. Hamas no longer poses a security threat, but as long as it holds territory, Israel retains a pretext for resuming the war. And as long as the Strip remains devastated and unlivable, the pressure on the people to leave only grows.” He added that Netanyahu’s defense minister, Israel Katz , after being criticized by a rival politician for not achieving a more decisive victory over Hamas, declared that the Israeli military was ready, if ordered, to eliminate Hamas “so that the emigration plan can be implemented.” 随后巴雷尔揭开了真正的故事：“加沙的僵局有利于以色列。哈马斯不再构成安全威胁，但只要它控制着领土，以色列就保留着恢复战争的借口。而只要加沙地带仍被毁坏、无法居住，民众离开的压力就只会增大。”他还说，在一名政敌批评未能对哈马斯取得更决定性胜利后，内塔尼亚胡的国防部长 以色列·卡茨 宣称，只要一声令下，以色列军方随时可以消灭哈马斯，“以便移民计划得以实施。” So that the emigration plan can be implemented. 以便移民计划得以实施。 Really? What is that? That is Orwellian speak for the ethnic cleansing of Gaza of Palestinians by the Netanyahu government. And what have Trump and his secretary of state, Marco Rubio, said in response? Zilch. 真的？那是什么？是内塔尼亚胡政府对加沙巴勒斯坦人进行种族清洗的奥威尔式说法。而特朗普和他的国务卿马可·鲁比奥对此作何回应？什么都没有。 I’ve learned over the years that diplomacy operates like a virus as well, beneficially or detrimentally: The more success you have, the more respect you get; the more respect you get, the more success you have. Conversely, the more failure you have, the less allies trust joining you, so the more failure you have. 这些年来我学到，外交也像病毒一样运作，不管是有益或有害：你越成功，得到的尊重越多；得到的尊重越多，你就越成功。反过来，越失败，盟友就越不愿加入你，于是你就越失败。 Example: Between March and October 1991, Secretary of State James A. Baker III made eight diplomatic trips to the Middle East to put together the Madrid peace conference — the first among Israel, the Palestine Liberation Organization and several Arab states. I made all eight trips with him as The Times’s diplomatic correspondent. He failed on the first seven, but Baker would not quit and he got it done on the eighth. 比如1991年3月至10月间，国务卿詹姆斯·A·贝克三世八次出访中东，促成马德里和会——这是以色列、巴勒斯坦解放组织和几个阿拉伯国家之间的首次和会。我作为时报外交记者随他八次出访。前七次他都失败了，但贝克没有放弃，第八次成功了。 Show me a single diplomatic initiative the Trump administration has built since the cease-fire in Gaza, which Trump has left to languish. It’s as if all he cared about was the headline from the signing, after which he amazingly declared last Oct. 13: “Together, we’ve achieved what everybody said was impossible. At long last we have peace in the Middle East.” 特朗普政府在加沙停火后促成了哪怕一项外交倡议吗？特朗普任由加沙在一片废墟之中。就好像他只在乎签字时的新闻报道，之后竟在去年10月13日 宣称 ：“我们共同实现了所有人都说不可能的事。中东终于有了和平。” Now that’s what I call a real hoax. 这才是我所说的真正骗局。 There is no energetic, focused follow-up because there are no clear lines of authority. You have Thomas Barrack, who is the special envoy for Syria and Iraq and the ambassador to Turkey, making his own policy statements . You have Massad Fares Boulos, the father-in-law of Trump’s daughter Tiffany, serving as a senior adviser to the president of the United States on Arab and Middle Eastern affairs. You have part-timers, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff. You have various assistant secretaries of state and defense. And you have Trump on his social media feed. (Somebody is going to make this into a musical!) 没有有力、专注的后续行动，是因为没有明确的权力链条。我们看到托马斯·巴拉克（叙利亚和伊拉克问题特使兼驻土耳其大使） 自己在发表政策声明 。看到马萨德·法雷斯·布洛斯（特朗普女儿蒂芙尼的公公）在担任美国总统的阿拉伯和中东事务 高级顾问 。看到兼职的贾里德·库什纳和史蒂夫·维特科夫。看到各种助理国务卿和助理国防部长。还有特朗普的社交媒体动态。（这些将来会被人写成一出音乐剧的！） What you don’t have is a secretary of state like Baker, relentlessly focusing and leveraging American power and making trip after trip after trip until he gets the job done. 我们没有看到的是，像贝克那样的国务卿，死咬着不放，并利用美国的力量，一次又一次出访，直到把事情办成。 The only thing Trump relentlessly follows up on is harassing the press. Last Saturday, after being forced by a judge to allow CNN reporters back in the White House after Trump illegally banned them because their coverage was not fawning enough, the president nevertheless blocked CNN from accompanying him on Air Force One to attend a football game in Tennessee. 而特朗普死咬着不放的是媒体。上周六，在一名法官迫使白宫允许CNN记者重返白宫之后——此前特朗普因他们的报道不够谄媚而非法禁止他们进入——总统还是禁止CNN随他乘坐空军一号前往田纳西州观看一场橄榄球赛。 When it comes to denouncing the press, Trump is laser-focused. But when dealing with the digital, biological and diplomatic viruses weakening our national immune system, not so much — to our great peril. 在谴责媒体方面，特朗普的注意力是高度集中的。但在应对削弱我们国家免疫系统的数字、生物和外交病毒时，就没那么专注了——而这将给我们带来巨大危险。 托马斯·L·弗里德曼(Thomas L. Friedman)是外交事务方面的专栏作者。他1981年加入时报，曾三次获得普利策奖。他著有七本书，包括赢得国家图书奖的《从贝鲁特到耶路撒冷》(From Beirut to Jerusalem)。欢迎在 X 和 Facebook 上关注他。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: OpenAI曾无视员工关于其人工智能安全问题的警告
description: SHEERA FRENKEL, DUSTIN VOLZ, DYLAN FREEDMAN2026年9月30日OpenAI首席执行官山姆·奥特曼。 Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times Months before OpenAI’s artificial intelligence went rogue, two employees raised an alarm with top executives. They were ignored. 在OpenAI人工智能失控前数月，两名员工曾向高层管理人员发出警告，但遭到忽视。 In emails, the employees said they worried that OpenAI’s newest artificial intelligence models were not being appropriately monitored during testing to gauge the technology’s sophistication and to secure the models, according to messages viewed by The New York Times. 据《纽约时报》查看的信息，这些员工在电子邮件中表示，他们担心OpenAI的最新人工智能模型在测试期间未得到适当监控，无法评估该技术的复杂程度并保护这些模型。 In response, OpenAI executives told the employees that the tests needed to move forward as quickly as possible to release the A.I. models on time. No additional security protocols were instituted, said the workers, who were not authorized to speak publicly on sensitive matters. 作为回应，OpenAI高管告诉这些员工，测试必须尽快推进，以便按时发布这些人工智能模型。这些未获敏感事项公开发言授权的员工说，公司没有实施额外的安全措施。 OpenAI’s models later broke out of their testing environments and attacked the A.I. start-up Hugging Face and other organizations, setting off a global debate about A.I. safety. OpenAI的模型后来突破了测试环境，攻击了人工智能初创公司Hugging Face和其他组织，引发了关于人工智能安全的全球辩论。 The exchanges between OpenAI employees and executives — which have not been previously reported — were part of a pattern where the San Francisco company did not prioritize security, according to employees and independent security researchers. That approach not only was evident with the testing of A.I. models, they said, but also showed up in other areas of the company, which makes the ChatGPT chatbot. 据员工和独立安全研究人员称，OpenAI员工与高管之间的这些此前未被报道的交流体现了这家旧金山公司不以安全为重的一贯作派。他们说，在这家制作了ChatGPT聊天机器人的公司内，不仅仅是人工智能模型的测试，其他的方面也能看到类似的问题。 Independent security researchers said they found bugs in recent months that allowed them to view the internal communications of OpenAI employees. They also found other vulnerabilities that would enable them to see the company’s internal computer code and view the chat logs of ChatGPT users. When the researchers contacted OpenAI about their findings, they said, the company initially disregarded them. 独立安全研究人员说，他们在最近几个月发现了漏洞，可以查看OpenAI员工的内部通信。他们还发现了其他漏洞，可以查看公司的内部计算机代码和ChatGPT用户的聊天记录。他们说，当研究人员就这些发现联系OpenAI时，该公司最初未予理会。 “OpenAI’s security seems to be about what you’d expect from a research lab that scaled at a blistering pace over four years and focused more on beating its competitors than securing its infrastructure,” said Joshua Saxe, the chief technology officer of the A.I. security firm Abundant Security. “OpenAI的安全状况基本上就是你能猜到的，一个在四年内以惊人速度扩张、更专注于击败竞争对手而非保护基础设施的研究实验室会有的样子，”人工智能安全公司Abundant Security的首席技术官约舒亚·萨克斯说。 OpenAI employees said that many of the day-to-day decisions about security were made by Greg Brockman, the company’s president, and Dane Stuckey, the chief information security officer. Sam Altman, the chief executive, is not closely involved in security, they said. OpenAI员工说，许多关于安全的日常决策由公司总裁格雷格·布罗克曼和首席信息安全官戴恩·斯塔基做出。他们说，首席执行官山姆·奥特曼并不密切参与安全事务。 OpenAI is not the only company that has recently disclosed A.I. security incidents. Google, Meta and Anthropic have also revealed that their most advanced A.I. technology escaped testing environments and autonomously attacked other computer infrastructure without their knowledge. OpenAI并非最近唯一披露人工智能安全事件的公司。谷歌、Meta和Anthropic也透露，它们最先进的人工智能技术逃出测试环境，并在它们不知情的情况下自主攻击了其他计算机基础设施。 But OpenAI’s handling of security is under particular scrutiny because its A.I. models have been involved in the biggest known number of instances of what the company has called “concerning” behavior — and in instances that experts have said were the most troubling. 但OpenAI对安全的处理尤其受到密切关注，因为其人工智能模型涉及被公司形容“令人担忧”的已知事件最多，也包括一些最令专家不安的事件。 In a dozen or so incidents, OpenAI’s systems hacked or tried to breach organizations, including the websites of U.S. government agencies; the technology also hid its mistakes, made up data, tried to message other chatbots and moved files onto the open internet without permission. In all of these cases, the A.I. acted without being instructed to do so. 在大约十几起事件中，OpenAI的系统入侵或试图入侵组织，包括美国政府机构的网站。该技术还隐藏错误、编造数据、试图向其他聊天机器人发送消息，并未经许可将文件移到开放互联网上。在所有这些案例中，人工智能都是在未被指示的情况下采取行动的。 “In some sense, this is an OpenAI-specific problem in that it seems like they had very bad security, and also sloppy model training practices that led to the models having this sort of propensity,” said Daniel Kokotajlo, a former OpenAI employee who has criticized the company’s safety and leads a research nonprofit called the AI Futures Project, though he added that other A.I. companies were not much better. “在某种意义上，这是OpenAI特有的问题，因为看起来他们的安全非常糟糕，模型训练操作也很草率，导致模型有这种倾向，”丹尼尔·科科塔伊洛说。他是一名曾批评该公司安全问题的前OpenAI员工，领导着一个名为AI Futures Project的非营利研究机构。不过他还补充说，其他人工智能公司也好不到哪里去。 “看起来他们的安全非常糟糕，”前OpenAI员工丹尼尔·科科塔伊洛这样评价这家AI公司。 Ian C. Bates for The New York Times Drew Pusateri, an OpenAI spokesman, said the company was committed to safety and took any security reports or concerns seriously. The lab has internal channels for reporting safety issues, he said, and took immediate action on flaws brought up by independent security researchers. OpenAI发言人德鲁·普萨特里说，公司致力于安全，并认真对待任何安全报告或担忧。他说，该实验室有报告安全问题的内部渠道，并对独立安全研究人员提出的缺陷立即采取行动。 “As frontier models have become more capable, we continue to evolve our security practices, but recognize a need to move faster,” Mr. Pusateri said. He added that OpenAI had slowed some A.I. development and was making changes to strengthen security in research and testing. “随着前沿模型能力越来越强，我们继续改进安全操作，但认识到需要更快行动，”普萨特里说。他还说，OpenAI已放缓一些人工智能开发，并正在做出改变，以加强研究和测试中的安全。 (The Times has sued OpenAI and Microsoft, claiming copyright infringement of news content related to A.I. systems. The two companies have denied those claims.) （《纽约时报》已起诉OpenAI和微软，主张其与人工智能系统相关的新闻内容版权受到侵犯。两家公司均予以否认。） Two OpenAI employees said workers had raised concerns for months about potential safety issues with testing A.I. models, including not enough monitoring. Employees also asked about vulnerabilities in the type of software the company was using to manage day-to-day safety, according to messages viewed by The Times. Each time, their questions were brushed aside or acted on too slowly, they said. 两名OpenAI员工说，员工们数月来一直对测试人工智能模型的潜在安全问题提出担忧，包括监控不足。据《纽约时报》查看的信息，员工们还询问了该公司用于管理日常安全的那类软件中的漏洞。他们说，每次他们的问题都被搁置或处理得太慢。 Security researchers said they had been met with a similar reception when they told OpenAI about other vulnerabilities. 安全研究人员说，当他们告诉OpenAI其他漏洞时，也受到类似对待。 In July, researchers at the security company Hacktron said they told OpenAI about how they had found a way to break into the company’s systems with the help of an A.I. model created by its rival Anthropic. OpenAI initially took issue with their approach, they said. 7月，安全公司Hacktron的研究人员说，他们告诉OpenAI，他们如何在其竞争对手Anthropic创建的人工智能模型帮助下找到了入侵该公司系统的方法。他们说，OpenAI最初对他们的做法表达了不满。 In a shared channel on the messaging platform Slack, Mr. Stuckey of OpenAI wrote that it was “pretty sad” that Hacktron’s researchers had gone to such lengths to demonstrate the company’s vulnerabilities, according to copies of the communications seen by The Times. 据《纽约时报》看到的通信副本，在消息平台Slack的一个共享频道中，OpenAI的斯塔基写道，Hacktron的研究人员如此大费周章地展示该公司的漏洞，“相当可悲。” “We just felt like they were angry at us,” Mohan Pedhapati, a Hacktron researcher, said of OpenAI. He added that the company appeared to still be using the security practices of a start-up, leveraging the software services of others for critical infrastructure instead of building its own tools. “我们只是觉得他们在生我们的气，”Hacktron研究员莫汉·佩达帕蒂在谈到OpenAI时说。他还说，该公司似乎仍在使用初创公司的安全操作，利用外部的软件服务来构建关键基础设施，而不是构建自己的工具。 “Why are you using Slack to build your nuclear Manhattan projects?” Mr. Pedhapati asked. Hacktron’s hack could have granted him full access to the Slack messaging platform to see what OpenAI employees were saying, he said. “你为什么要用Slack来构建你的曼哈顿核计划？”佩达帕蒂问道。他说，Hacktron的黑客攻击可以做到获取Slack消息平台的完全权限，让他看到OpenAI员工在说什么。 Mr. Stuckey later apologized to Hacktron, and OpenAI awarded the researchers $6,500 for disclosing the flaw. 斯塔基后来向Hacktron道歉，OpenAI向披露该漏洞的研究人员提供了6500美元作为奖励。 “We thank the researchers for contacting us and sharing their findings,” Mr. Pusateri said. On Friday, an independent report released by a group of engineers and researchers revealed new alarming behavior from the Hugging Face incident, including instances in which OpenAI’s agents tried to message Anthropic’s Claude and use other A.I. models to beat anti-robot protections on a website. “我们感谢研究人员联系我们并分享他们的发现，”普萨特里说。周五，一个工程师和研究人员团队发布了一份独立报告，揭示了有关Hugging Face事件的一些令人震惊的新发现，包括OpenAI的智能体试图向Anthropic的Claude发送消息，并使用其他人工智能模型来绕过网站上的反机器人保护。 OpenAI revealed last week that new safeguards had failed to prevent its latest A.I. model from breaking through them to gain access to the internet. A retrospective review found other instances of unauthorized internet access that had gone undetected. OpenAI announced that it was pausing training for its most advanced models and was engaged in an extensive review of unexpected behavior by the technology. OpenAI上周透露，新的保障措施未能阻止其最新人工智能模型获取互联网访问权限。一项回溯审查发现了一些此前未发现的未经授权访问互联网事件。OpenAI宣布暂停其最先进模型的训练，并对该技术的意外行为进行广泛审查。 研究人员向OpenAI报告了一个漏洞，该漏洞可能允许人们访问ChatGPT用户的全部私人聊天记录。 Eric Helgas for The New York Times On Monday, the company went even further. It said it would not release its newest A.I. model, GPT-6.1 Astra, because of security concerns raised by its researchers. 周一，该公司更进一步，表示鉴于研究人员提出了安全担忧，不会发布其最新人工智能模型GPT-6.1 Astra。 Sheera Frenkel是《纽约时报》记者，常驻旧金山湾区，报道国防和监控技术。 Dustin Volz为时报撰写网络安全和情报方面的文章，他常驻华盛顿。 Dylan Freedman是时报人工智能项目编辑，负责调查各种相关话题。他兼具记者与机器学习工程师的双重工作经验。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。
