No additional security protocols were instituted, said the workers, who were not authorized to speak publicly on sensitive matters. 作为回应，OpenAI高管告诉这些员工，测试必须尽快推进，以便按时发布这些人工智能模型。这些未获敏感事项公开发言授权的员工说，公司没有实施额外的安全措施。 OpenAI’s models later broke out of their testing environments and attacked the A.I. start-up Hugging Face and other organizations, setting off a global debate about A.I. safety . OpenAI的模型后来突破了测试环境， 攻击了人工智能初创公司Hugging Face 和其他组织，引发了 关于人工智能安全的全球辩论 。 The exchanges between OpenAI employees and executives — which have not been previously reported — were part of a pattern where the San Francisco company did not prioritize security, according to employees and independent security researchers. That approach not only was evident with the testing of A.I. models, they said, but also showed up in other areas of the company, which makes the ChatGPT chatbot. 据员工和独立安全研究人员称，OpenAI员工与高管之间的这些此前未被报道的交流体现了这家旧金山公司不以安全为重的一贯作派。他们说，在这家制作了ChatGPT聊天机器人的公司内，不仅仅是人工智能模型的测试，其他的方面也能看到类似的问题。 Independent security researchers said they found bugs in recent months that allowed them to view the internal communications of OpenAI employees. They also found other vulnerabilities that would enable them to see the company’s internal computer code and view the chat logs of ChatGPT users. When the researchers contacted OpenAI about their findings, they said, the company initially disregarded them. 独立安全研究人员说，他们在最近几个月发现了漏洞，可以查看OpenAI员工的内部通信。他们还发现了其他漏洞，可以查看公司的内部计算机代码和ChatGPT用户的聊天记录。他们说，当研究人员就这些发现联系OpenAI时，该公司最初未予理会。 “OpenAI’s security seems to be about what you’d expect from a research lab that scaled at a blistering pace over four years and focused more on beating its competitors than securing its infrastructure,” said Joshua Saxe, the chief technology officer of the A.I. security firm Abundant Security. “OpenAI的安全状况基本上就是你能猜到的，一个在四年内以惊人速度扩张、更专注于击败竞争对手而非保护基础设施的研究实验室会有的样子，”人工智能安全公司Abundant Security的首席技术官约舒亚·萨克斯说。 OpenAI employees said that many of the day-to-day decisions about security were made by Greg Brockman, the company’s president, and Dane Stuckey, the chief information security officer. Sam Altman, the chief executive, is not closely involved in security, they said. OpenAI员工说，许多关于安全的日常决策由公司总裁格雷格·布罗克曼和首席信息安全官戴恩·斯塔基做出。他们说，首席执行官山姆·奥特曼并不密切参与安全事务。 OpenAI is not the only company that has recently disclosed A.I. security incidents. Google, Meta and Anthropic have also revealed that their most advanced A.I. technology escaped testing environments and autonomously attacked other computer infrastructure without their knowledge. OpenAI并非最近唯一披露人工智能安全事件的公司。谷歌、Meta和Anthropic也透露，它们最先进的人工智能技术逃出测试环境，并在它们不知情的情况下自主攻击了其他计算机基础设施。 But OpenAI’s handling of security is under particular scrutiny because its A.I. models have been involved in the biggest known number of instances of what the company has called “concerning” behavior — and in instances that experts have said were the most troubling. 但OpenAI对安全的处理尤其受到密切关注，因为其人工智能模型涉及被公司形容“令人担忧”的已知事件最多，也包括一些最令专家不安的事件。 In a dozen or so incidents, OpenAI’s systems hacked or tried to breach organizations, including the websites of U.S. government agencies ; the technology also hid its mistakes, made up data, tried to message other chatbots and moved files onto the open internet without permission. In all of these cases, the A.I. acted without being instructed to do so. 在大约十几起事件中，OpenAI的系统入侵或试图入侵组织，包括 美国政府机构的网站 。该技术还隐藏错误、编造数据、试图向其他聊天机器人发送消息，并未经许可将文件移到开放互联网上。在所有这些案例中，人工智能都是在未被指示的情况下采取行动的。 “In some sense, this is an OpenAI-specific problem in that it seems like they had very bad security, and also sloppy model training practices that led to the models having this sort of propensity,” said Daniel Kokotajlo, a former OpenAI employee who has criticized the company’s safety and leads a research nonprofit called the AI Futures Project, though he added that other A.I. companies were not much better. “在某种意义上，这是OpenAI特有的问题，因为看起来他们的安全非常糟糕，模型训练操作也很草率，导致模型有这种倾向，”丹尼尔·科科塔伊洛说。他是一名曾批评该公司安全问题的前 OpenAI员工 ，领导着一个名为AI Futures Project的非营利研究机构。不过他还补充说，其他人工智能公司也好不到哪里去。 “看起来他们的安全非常糟糕，”前OpenAI员工丹尼尔·科科塔伊洛这样评价这家AI公司。 Ian C. Bates for The New York Times Drew Pusateri, an OpenAI spokesman, said the company was committed to safety and took any security reports or concerns seriously. The lab has internal channels for reporting safety issues, he said, and took immediate action on flaws brought up by independent security researchers. OpenAI发言人德鲁·普萨特里说，公司致力于安全，并认真对待任何安全报告或担忧。他说，该实验室有报告安全问题的内部渠道，并对独立安全研究人员提出的缺陷立即采取行动。 “As frontier models have become more capable, we continue to evolve our security practices, but recognize a need to move faster,” Mr. Pusateri said. He added that OpenAI had slowed some A.I. development and was making changes to strengthen security in research and testing. “随着前沿模型能力越来越强，我们继续改进安全操作，但认识到需要更快行动，”普萨特里说。他还说，OpenAI已放缓一些人工智能开发，并正在做出改变，以加强研究和测试中的安全。 (The Times has sued OpenAI and Microsoft , claiming copyright infringement of news content related to A.I. systems. The two companies have denied those claims.) （《纽约时报》已 起诉OpenAI和微软 ，主张其与人工智能系统相关的新闻内容版权受到侵犯。两家公司均予以否认。） Two OpenAI employees said workers had raised concerns for months about potential safety issues with testing A.I. models, including not enough monitoring. Employees also asked about vulnerabilities in the type of software the company was using to manage day-to-day safety, according to messages viewed by The Times. Each time, their questions were brushed aside or acted on too slowly, they said. 两名OpenAI员工说，员工们数月来一直对测试人工智能模型的潜在安全问题提出担忧，包括监控不足。据《纽约时报》查看的信息，员工们还询问了该公司用于管理日常安全的那类软件中的漏洞。他们说，每次他们的问题都被搁置或处理得太慢。 Security researchers said they had been met with a similar reception when they told OpenAI about other vulnerabilities. 安全研究人员说，当他们告诉OpenAI其他漏洞时，也受到类似对待。 In July, researchers at the security company Hacktron said they told OpenAI about how they had found a way to break into the company’s systems with the help of an A.I. model created by its rival Anthropic. OpenAI initially took issue with their approach, they said. 7月，安全公司Hacktron的研究人员说，他们告诉OpenAI，他们如何在其竞争对手Anthropic创建的人工智能模型帮助下 找到了入侵该公司系统的方法 。他们说，OpenAI最初对他们的做法表达了不满。 In a shared channel on the messaging platform Slack, Mr. Stuckey of OpenAI wrote that it was “pretty sad” that Hacktron’s researchers had gone to such lengths to demonstrate the company’s vulnerabilities, according to copies of the communications seen by The Times. 据《纽约时报》看到的通信副本，在消息平台Slack的一个共享频道中，OpenAI的斯塔基写道，Hacktron的研究人员如此大费周章地展示该公司的漏洞，“相当可悲。” “We just felt like they were angry at us,” Mohan Pedhapati, a Hacktron researcher, said of OpenAI. He added that the company appeared to still be using the security practices of a start-up, leveraging the software services of others for critical infrastructure instead of building its own tools. “我们只是觉得他们在生我们的气，”Hacktron研究员莫汉·佩达帕蒂在谈到OpenAI时说。他还说，该公司似乎仍在使用初创公司的安全操作，利用外部的软件服务来构建关键基础设施，而不是构建自己的工具。 “Why are you using Slack to build your nuclear Manhattan projects?” Mr. Pedhapati asked. Hacktron’s hack could have granted him full access to the Slack messaging platform to see what OpenAI employees were saying, he said. “你为什么要用Slack来构建你的曼哈顿核计划？”佩达帕蒂问道。他说，Hacktron的黑客攻击可以做到获取Slack消息平台的完全权限，让他看到OpenAI员工在说什么。 Mr. Stuckey later apologized to Hacktron, and OpenAI awarded the researchers $6,500 for disclosing the flaw. 斯塔基后来向Hacktron道歉，OpenAI向披露该漏洞的研究人员提供了6500美元作为奖励。 “We thank the researchers for contacting us and sharing their finding s, ” Mr. Pusateri said. On Friday, an independent report released by a group of engineers and researchers revealed new alarming behavior from the Hugging Face incident, including instances in which OpenAI’s agents tried to message Anthropic’s Claude and use other A.I. models to beat anti-robot protections on a website. “我们感谢研究人员联系我们并分享他们的发现，”普萨特里说。周五，一个工程师和研究人员团队发布了一份 独立报告 ，揭示了有关Hugging Face事件的一些令人震惊的新发现，包括OpenAI的智能体试图向Anthropic的Claude发送消息，并使用其他人工智能模型来绕过网站上的反机器人保护。 OpenAI revealed last week that new safeguards had failed to prevent its latest A.I. model from breaking through them to gain access to the internet. A retrospective review found other instances of unauthorized internet access that had gone undetected. OpenAI announced that it was pausing training for its most advanced models and was engaged in an extensive review of unexpected behavior by the technology. OpenAI上周 透露 ，新的保障措施未能阻止其最新人工智能模型获取互联网访问权限。一项回溯审查发现了一些此前未发现的未经授权访问互联网事件。OpenAI宣布暂停其最先进模型的训练，并对该技术的意外行为进行广泛审查。 研究人员向OpenAI报告了一个漏洞，该漏洞可能允许人们访问ChatGPT用户的全部私人聊天记录。 Eric Helgas for The New York Times On Monday, the company went even further. It said it would not release its newest A.I. model, GPT-6.1 Astra , because of security concerns raised by its researchers. 周一，该公司更进一步，表示鉴于研究人员提出了安全担忧，不会发布其最新人工智能模型 GPT-6.1 Astra 。 Sheera Frenkel 是《纽约时报》记者，常驻旧金山湾区，报道国防和监控技术。 Dustin Volz 为时报撰写网络安全和情报方面的文章，他常驻华盛顿。 Dylan Freedman 是时报人工智能项目编辑，负责调查各种相关话题。他兼具记者与机器学习工程师的双重工作经验。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 康奈尔大学兄弟会强奸案调查重启：目前我们所知的
description: SHARON OTTERMAN2026年9月30日康奈尔大学的Chi Phi兄弟会会舍，现已关闭。 Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times Prosecutors have reopened an investigation into a 2024 report by a Cornell University student who said she was raped at a fraternity house, raising questions about how the case was initially handled by law enforcement officials and the school. 检方重新启动了对康奈尔大学一名学生2024年报案称自己在兄弟会会舍遭强奸一案的调查，这也引发了外界对执法部门和学校当初对此案处理的质疑。 Her allegations surfaced again two weeks ago after the student, identified as Jane Doe in a lawsuit, sued seven men, the university, her sorority and the fraternity. The case has led to fierce debate across the internet and drawn attention to the persistent problem of sexual assault on college campuses. 两周前，这名学生——在诉讼中以“无名氏”代称——起诉了七名男子、康奈尔大学、她所在的姐妹会以及涉事兄弟会，她的指控因此再次浮出水面。此案在网上引发激烈争论，也让大学校园性侵这一长期存在的问题再度受到关注。 The district attorney for Tompkins County, home to Cornell in Ithaca, N.Y., said he would consider presenting the case to a grand jury. In 2024, immediately after her report, he declined to do so. 纽约州汤普金斯县（康奈尔大学位于该县的伊萨卡市）地方检察官表示，他会考虑将案件提交大陪审团。而在2024年，也就是这名学生报案后不久，他曾决定不这样做。 Here’s what we know about the Cornell case. 以下是我们目前了解到的康奈尔大学这起案件的相关情况。 What do we know about Jane Doe? 关于“无名氏”的情况 Because she is anonymous in the lawsuit, most of the details about her life are unknown. Her lawyer has said she is from a small town, about 1,000 miles away from Cornell. She arrived at the university as an undergraduate in August 2022, then dropped out after she said she was raped in 2024. She was 20 years old at the time and had been a member of the Tri-Delta sorority. 由于她在诉讼中匿名，关于她生活的大部分细节都不为人知。她的律师说，她来自一个距离康奈尔大学约1600公里的小镇。她于2022年8月进入康奈尔大学读本科，在2024年声称自己遭到强奸后退学。当时她20岁，是Tri-Delta姐妹会成员。 Her lawyer said she is struggling now with the aftermath of the incident and not in college. 律师说，她目前仍在应对事件带来的后续影响，也没有继续上大学。 What does the lawsuit say happened? 诉讼对事情经过的描述 On Oct. 19, 2024, according to the lawsuit, the woman was raped repeatedly over nearly seven hours at the Chi Phi fraternity house in Ithaca, N.Y. 根据诉讼，2024年10月19日，这名女子在纽约州伊萨卡的Chi Phi兄弟会会舍内多次遭到强奸，持续了近七个小时。 The lawsuit states that she started off her night drinking vodka at the sorority house. At around 8:30 p.m., she took an Uber to an event her sorority was hosting at a bar. Although the bouncer correctly identified her as underage, she claims she was served at least one alcoholic beverage. By about 11 p.m., she had decided to walk about a mile to Chi Phi’s fraternity house to see a man she considered a friend. 诉讼称，她当晚先在姐妹会会舍喝了伏特加。晚上8点30分左右，她乘Uber前往姐妹会在某酒吧举办的一场活动。虽然保镖正确识别出她未达法定饮酒年龄，但她声称，自己仍被提供了至少一杯酒精饮料。到晚上11点左右，她决定步行约1.6公里前往Chi Ph兄弟会会舍，去见一名她视为朋友的男子。 Once she arrived, according to the lawsuit, the man and his fraternity brothers gave her a beer, marijuana, rum and ketamine. In the lawsuit, she claims she had not tried ketamine before and was pressured into snorting it. The lawsuit then details a series of sexual assaults and continued drug use involving her friend and six other men. 诉讼称，她抵达后，那名男子和他的兄弟会兄弟给了她啤酒、大麻、朗姆酒和氯胺酮（俗称K粉）。她在诉讼中称，自己以前从未用过K粉，是被迫吸食的。诉讼随后详细描述了一系列性侵行为，以及她与这名朋友和其他六名男子持续使用毒品的情况。 At about 1:42 a.m., one of the men sent a message to the Chi Phi Snapchat group inviting others to join in, using a crude name for female genitalia, according to a screenshot included in the lawsuit. 诉讼所附的一张截图显示，凌晨1点42分左右，其中一名男子在Chi Phi兄弟会的 Snapchat群组里发消息邀其他人加入，并使用了女性生殖器的粗俗称呼。 How did the police respond? 警方的回应 With the encouragement of friends, Jane Doe reported the incident to Cornell’s police department on Nov. 8, 2024. 在朋友们的鼓励下，“无名氏”于2024年11月8日向康奈尔大学警察局报案。 The Cornell police sent a crime alert to campus, stating that a victim had reported being “sexually assaulted by several males and coerced into consuming ketamine and other drugs” at a fraternity house. In a message to campus before that Thanksgiving, Cornell’s president said that the university police department was continuing its criminal investigation, and that a second, administrative investigation into the allegations was underway. 康奈尔警方向校园发布犯罪警报，称一名受害者报告自己在兄弟会会舍“遭多名男性性侵，并被强迫吸食氯胺酮和其他毒品”。在那个感恩节前发给校园的信息中，康奈尔校长表示，大学警察局正在继续刑事调查，同时针对这些指控的第二项行政调查也在进行中。 Some time that month, Cornell police asked the Tompkins County district attorney’s office to review a statement from Jane Doe. Criminal investigators advised the police that they did not think they could bring criminal charges under New York State law based on the statement. Jane Doe’s lawyer said that after she gave her initial statement, no police or criminal investigators ever contacted her again. 当月某个时候，康奈尔警方要求汤普金斯县地方检察官办公室审查“无名氏”的一份陈述。刑事调查人员告知警方，他们认为根据纽约州法律，仅凭这份陈述无法提起刑事指控。“无名氏”的律师说，她作出最初陈述后，再也没有任何警察或刑事调查人员联系过她。 It is unclear whether the police interviewed the men involved, or whether Jane Doe was ever told that her criminal case was not being pursued. 目前尚不清楚警方是否讯问过涉案男子，也不清楚“无名氏”是否曾被告知，她的刑事案件不会继续推进。 On Monday, the district attorney — who has released only excerpts from Jane Doe’s initial six-page statement — said that the statement did not make clear that she was forced into the sexual acts, or that she was incapacitated, though she was under the influence of drugs and alcohol. 周一，地方检察官表示——他目前只公布了“无名氏”最初那份六页陈述中的部分内容——该陈述没有明确表明她是被迫发生性行为的，也没有明确表明她当时已丧失行为能力，尽管她当时确实受到毒品和酒精影响。 How did Cornell respond? 康奈尔大学当时的回应 The university immediately placed the fraternity, and the seven men she named in the lawsuit, on interim suspensions, the suit said. 诉讼称，校方立即对涉事兄弟会以及她在诉讼中点名的七名男子作出临时停学处理。 Meanwhile, Cornell’s administrative Title IX justice process swung into motion to determine any potential discipline for the accused men. In May 2025, at least 12 hearings were held before a panel of faculty and staff, according to the woman’s lawsuit. 与此同时，康奈尔大学依据《教育法修正案第九条》开展的校内行政程序也随即启动，以决定是否应对这些被指控的男子作出处分。根据这名女子的诉讼，2025年5月，由教职员工组成的一个审议小组举行了至少12场听证。 The accused men “were afforded the opportunity to mitigate their conduct by submitting essays to Cornell,” according to the lawsuit. Cornell does not deny that essays — which it calls reflection papers — were part of the punishment that the panel decided on for some of the men. But it stated Monday that it was not the only consequence for any of them. 诉讼称，被告男子“获得了通过向康奈尔提交书面材料来减轻其行为后果的机会”。康奈尔并不否认这些书面材料——校方称之为检讨——是小组决定对部分男子实施的处罚之一。但校方周一表示，对于任何一个当事人来说，这并非唯一的处分。 Cornell, citing student privacy rules, declined to give details about how the individual men were punished. It said Monday that it gave the men “a range of sanctions, which included expulsions and suspensions.” Thomas Giuffra, the lawyer who represents Jane Doe, has said in interviews that only two of the men were expelled, and that his client did not feel justice had been done. 康奈尔大学以学生隐私规定为由，拒绝透露对这些男子各自的具体处分。校方周一表示，对他们采取了“一系列处分措施，其中包括开除和停学”。代表“无名氏”的律师托马斯·朱弗拉在采访中称，只有两名男子被开除，而他的当事人认为正义并未得到伸张。 What has been the fallout so far from the lawsuit? 此案的反响 Millions of people have viewed the lawsuit or heard influencers and celebrities talk about the allegations online, bringing attention to the ongoing problem of sexual assault at Cornell and other college campuses. The mayor of Ithaca said Monday that he is proposing a ban on permits for Cornell events until the university reforms its sexual assault policies. 已有数百万人看过这份诉讼文件，或在网上听网红和名人谈论这些指控，这令康奈尔大学以及其他大学校园长期存在的性侵问题受到更多关注。伊萨卡市市长周一表示，他将提议，在康奈尔大学对性侵事件处理政策进行改革之前，禁止批准该校的活动举办许可。 The pressure and attention pushed the Tompkins County district attorney to reopen the criminal case. A criminal investigator has reached out to Jane Doe’s lawyer, meaning that there could still be criminal charges in the case. Gov. Kathy Hochul has called for an independent investigation of Cornell’s handling of the case. 舆论压力和关注促使汤普金斯县地方检察官重启刑事调查。一名刑事调查人员已经联系了“无名氏”的律师，这意味着此案仍有可能提出刑事指控。纽约州州长凯西·霍格尔已要求对康奈尔大学处理此案的方式展开独立调查。 The names and photographs of the seven accused men are widely circulating online, as part of a mass movement that some see as a grass-roots effort to bring accountability, and others view as a form of harassment of men not yet charged with any crime. 七名被告男子的姓名和照片在网上广泛传播。有人将这场大规模行动视为草根式的追责努力，也有人认为这是对尚未被控任何罪名的男子的骚扰。 Hurubie Meko对本文有报道贡献。 Sharon Otterman是《纽约时报》记者，报道高等教育、公共卫生以及纽约市面临的其他问题。 翻译：杜然 点击查看本文英文版。
content: SHARON OTTERMAN 2026年9月30日 康奈尔大学的Chi Phi兄弟会会舍，现已关闭。 Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times Prosecutors have reopened an investigation into a 2024 report by a Cornell University student who said she was raped at a fraternity house, raising questions about how the case was initially handled by law enforcement officials and the school. 检方重新启动了对康奈尔大学一名学生2024年报案称自己在兄弟会会舍遭强奸一案的调查，这也引发了外界对执法部门和学校当初对此案处理的质疑。 Her allegations surfaced again two weeks ago after the student, identified as Jane Doe in a lawsuit, sued seven men, the university, her sorority and the fraternity. The case has led to fierce debate across the internet and drawn attention to the persistent problem of sexual assault on college campuses. 两周前，这名学生——在诉讼中以“无名氏”代称——起诉了七名男子、康奈尔大学、她所在的姐妹会以及涉事兄弟会，她的指控因此再次浮出水面。此案在网上引发激烈争论，也让大学校园性侵这一长期存在的问题再度受到关注。 The district attorney for Tompkins County, home to Cornell in Ithaca, N.Y., said he would consider presenting the case to a grand jury. In 2024, immediately after her report, he declined to do so. 纽约州汤普金斯县（康奈尔大学位于该县的伊萨卡市）地方检察官表示，他会考虑将案件提交大陪审团。而在2024年，也就是这名学生报案后不久，他曾决定不这样做。 Here’s what we know about the Cornell case. 以下是我们目前了解到的康奈尔大学这起案件的相关情况。 What do we know about Jane Doe? 关于“无名氏”的情况 Because she is anonymous in the lawsuit, most of the details about her life are unknown. Her lawyer has said she is from a small town, about 1,000 miles away from Cornell. She arrived at the university as an undergraduate in August 2022, then dropped out after she said she was raped in 2024. She was 20 years old at the time and had been a member of the Tri-Delta sorority. 由于她在诉讼中匿名，关于她生活的大部分细节都不为人知。她的律师说，她来自一个距离康奈尔大学约1600公里的小镇。她于2022年8月进入康奈尔大学读本科，在2024年声称自己遭到强奸后退学。当时她20岁，是Tri-Delta姐妹会成员。 Her lawyer said she is struggling now with the aftermath of the incident and not in college. 律师说，她目前仍在应对事件带来的后续影响，也没有继续上大学。 What does the lawsuit say happened? 诉讼对事情经过的描述 On Oct. 19, 2024, according to the lawsuit, the woman was raped repeatedly over nearly seven hours at the Chi Phi fraternity house in Ithaca, N.Y. 根据诉讼，2024年10月19日，这名女子在纽约州伊萨卡的Chi Phi兄弟会会舍内多次遭到强奸，持续了近七个小时。 The lawsuit states that she started off her night drinking vodka at the sorority house. At around 8:30 p.m., she took an Uber to an event her sorority was hosting at a bar. Although the bouncer correctly identified her as underage, she claims she was served at least one alcoholic beverage. By about 11 p.m., she had decided to walk about a mile to Chi Phi’s fraternity house to see a man she considered a friend. 诉讼称，她当晚先在姐妹会会舍喝了伏特加。晚上8点30分左右，她乘Uber前往姐妹会在某酒吧举办的一场活动。虽然保镖正确识别出她未达法定饮酒年龄，但她声称，自己仍被提供了至少一杯酒精饮料。到晚上11点左右，她决定步行约1.6公里前往Chi Ph兄弟会会舍，去见一名她视为朋友的男子。 Once she arrived, according to the lawsuit, the man and his fraternity brothers gave her a beer, marijuana, rum and ketamine. In the lawsuit, she claims she had not tried ketamine before and was pressured into snorting it. The lawsuit then details a series of sexual assaults and continued drug use involving her friend and six other men. 诉讼称，她抵达后，那名男子和他的兄弟会兄弟给了她啤酒、大麻、朗姆酒和氯胺酮（俗称K粉）。她在诉讼中称，自己以前从未用过K粉，是被迫吸食的。诉讼随后详细描述了一系列性侵行为，以及她与这名朋友和其他六名男子持续使用毒品的情况。 At about 1:42 a.m., one of the men sent a message to the Chi Phi Snapchat group inviting others to join in, using a crude name for female genitalia, according to a screenshot included in the lawsuit. 诉讼所附的一张截图显示，凌晨1点42分左右，其中一名男子在Chi Phi兄弟会的 Snapchat群组里发消息邀其他人加入，并使用了女性生殖器的粗俗称呼。 How did the police respond? 警方的回应 With the encouragement of friends, Jane Doe reported the incident to Cornell’s police department on Nov. 8, 2024. 在朋友们的鼓励下，“无名氏”于2024年11月8日向康奈尔大学警察局报案。 The Cornell police sent a crime alert to campus, stating that a victim had reported being “sexually assaulted by several males and coerced into consuming ketamine and other drugs” at a fraternity house. In a message to campus before that Thanksgiving, Cornell’s president said that the university police department was continuing its criminal investigation, and that a second, administrative investigation into the allegations was underway. 康奈尔警方向校园发布犯罪警报，称一名受害者报告自己在兄弟会会舍“遭多名男性性侵，并被强迫吸食氯胺酮和其他毒品”。在那个感恩节前发给校园的信息中，康奈尔校长表示，大学警察局正在继续刑事调查，同时针对这些指控的第二项行政调查也在进行中。 Some time that month, Cornell police asked the Tompkins County district attorney’s office to review a statement from Jane Doe. Criminal investigators advised the police that they did not think they could bring criminal charges under New York State law based on the statement. Jane Doe’s lawyer said that after she gave her initial statement, no police or criminal investigators ever contacted her again. 当月某个时候，康奈尔警方要求汤普金斯县地方检察官办公室审查“无名氏”的一份陈述。刑事调查人员告知警方，他们认为根据纽约州法律，仅凭这份陈述无法提起刑事指控。“无名氏”的律师说，她作出最初陈述后，再也没有任何警察或刑事调查人员联系过她。 It is unclear whether the police interviewed the men involved, or whether Jane Doe was ever told that her criminal case was not being pursued. 目前尚不清楚警方是否讯问过涉案男子，也不清楚“无名氏”是否曾被告知，她的刑事案件不会继续推进。 On Monday, the district attorney — who has released only excerpts from Jane Doe’s initial six-page statement — said that the statement did not make clear that she was forced into the sexual acts, or that she was incapacitated, though she was under the influence of drugs and alcohol. 周一，地方检察官表示——他目前只公布了“无名氏”最初那份六页陈述中的部分内容——该陈述没有明确表明她是被迫发生性行为的，也没有明确表明她当时已丧失行为能力，尽管她当时确实受到毒品和酒精影响。 How did Cornell respond? 康奈尔大学当时的回应 The university immediately placed the fraternity, and the seven men she named in the lawsuit, on interim suspensions, the suit said. 诉讼称，校方立即对涉事兄弟会以及她在诉讼中点名的七名男子作出临时停学处理。 Meanwhile, Cornell’s administrative Title IX justice process swung into motion to determine any potential discipline for the accused men. In May 2025, at least 12 hearings were held before a panel of faculty and staff, according to the woman’s lawsuit. 与此同时，康奈尔大学依据《教育法修正案第九条》开展的校内行政程序也随即启动，以决定是否应对这些被指控的男子作出处分。根据这名女子的诉讼，2025年5月，由教职员工组成的一个审议小组举行了至少12场听证。 The accused men “were afforded the opportunity to mitigate their conduct by submitting essays to Cornell,” according to the lawsuit. Cornell does not deny that essays — which it calls reflection papers — were part of the punishment that the panel decided on for some of the men. But it stated Monday that it was not the only consequence for any of them. 诉讼称，被告男子“获得了通过向康奈尔提交书面材料来减轻其行为后果的机会”。康奈尔并不否认这些书面材料——校方称之为检讨——是小组决定对部分男子实施的处罚之一。但校方周一表示，对于任何一个当事人来说，这并非唯一的处分。 Cornell, citing student privacy rules, declined to give details about how the individual men were punished. It said Monday that it gave the men “a range of sanctions, which included expulsions and suspensions.” Thomas Giuffra, the lawyer who represents Jane Doe, has said in interviews that only two of the men were expelled, and that his client did not feel justice had been done. 康奈尔大学以学生隐私规定为由，拒绝透露对这些男子各自的具体处分。校方周一表示，对他们采取了“一系列处分措施，其中包括开除和停学”。代表“无名氏”的律师托马斯·朱弗拉在采访中称，只有两名男子被开除，而他的当事人认为正义并未得到伸张。 What has been the fallout so far from the lawsuit? 此案的反响 Millions of people have viewed the lawsuit or heard influencers and celebrities talk about the allegations online, bringing attention to the ongoing problem of sexual assault at Cornell and other college campuses. The mayor of Ithaca said Monday that he is proposing a ban on permits for Cornell events until the university reforms its sexual assault policies. 已有数百万人看过这份诉讼文件，或在网上听网红和名人谈论这些指控，这令康奈尔大学以及其他大学校园长期存在的性侵问题受到更多关注。伊萨卡市市长周一表示，他将提议，在康奈尔大学对性侵事件处理政策进行改革之前，禁止批准该校的活动举办许可。 The pressure and attention pushed the Tompkins County district attorney to reopen the criminal case. A criminal investigator has reached out to Jane Doe’s lawyer, meaning that there could still be criminal charges in the case. Gov. Kathy Hochul has called for an independent investigation of Cornell’s handling of the case. 舆论压力和关注促使汤普金斯县地方检察官重启刑事调查。一名刑事调查人员已经联系了“无名氏”的律师，这意味着此案仍有可能提出刑事指控。纽约州州长凯西·霍格尔已要求对康奈尔大学处理此案的方式展开独立调查。 The names and photographs of the seven accused men are widely circulating online, as part of a mass movement that some see as a grass-roots effort to bring accountability, and others view as a form of harassment of men not yet charged with any crime. 七名被告男子的姓名和照片在网上广泛传播。有人将这场大规模行动视为草根式的追责努力，也有人认为这是对尚未被控任何罪名的男子的骚扰。 Hurubie Meko对本文有报道贡献。 Sharon Otterman是《纽约时报》记者，报道高等教育、公共卫生以及纽约市面临的其他问题。 翻译：杜然 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 特朗普要求人工智能巨头自我监管
description: KATIE ROGERS, CECILIA KANG2026年9月30日周二，特朗普总统在白宫向公众推出一个由人工智能驱动的政府网站。 Doug Mills/The New York Times President Trump summoned the world’s most powerful technology executives to the White House on Tuesday, and praised the assembled billionaires as “very brilliant” minds who wanted to make the world a better place through job creation, the construction of data centers and the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence. 特朗普总统周二将全球最有权势的科技高管召集到白宫，称赞与会的亿万富翁们是“非常杰出”的人才，称他们希望通过创造就业机会、建设数据中心以及快速扩张人工智能让世界变得更美好。 As president, Mr. Trump faces questions about whether A.I. should be regulated, and particularly whether restrictions should be put in place to protect humans from technology that has learned to outmaneuver existing safeguards. 作为总统，特朗普面临着人工智能是否应该受到监管的质询，特别是是否应该实施限制措施，避免人类受到已学会规避现有安全防护措施的技术的伤害。 But in the end, convening all of those billions and all of that brain power did not result in a commitment to formal regulation. Instead, they signed a voluntary agreement to adopt safety policies that include risk reviews, auditing and evaluations of systems by third parties. They also agreed to adopt Mr. Trump’s preferred rebranding of A.I.: “super intelligence.” 但最终，召集这些亿万富翁和顶尖大脑并没有带来对正式监管的承诺。取而代之的是，他们签署了一项自愿协议，承诺采取安全政策，包括由第三方对系统进行风险审查、审计和评估。他们还同意采用特朗普偏爱的人工智能新名称：“超级智能”。 “This is going to be all for the good, and we’re going to have it be nice and safe,” Mr. Trump said on Tuesday afternoon, when he and the tech leaders took questions outside the White House. “And they’re really going to be policing each other, and that’s the way it works.” “这一切都将是为了更好的未来，我们将让它变得美好且安全，”特朗普在周二下午与科技领袖们在白宫外接受提问时说道。“而且他们真的会互相监督，这就是它的运作方式。” Asked if the agreement would be binding, Mr. Trump said, “I think it’s morally binding.” 当被问及该协议是否具有约束力时，特朗普说：“我认为它具有道德约束力。” Inside the White House luncheon, Mr. Trump’s seating chart (which he posted on social media) revealed a powerful assemblage of executives who are deeply divided on the need for A.I. safeguards. The meeting also included top officials, such as Speaker Mike Johnson and Vice President JD Vance, who believe that formalized safeguards would hurt American competitiveness. 在白宫午餐会上，特朗普公布的座位表（由他本人发布在社交媒体上）显示，与会的高管们实力雄厚，但在是否需要制定人工智能保障措施的问题上存在严重分歧。与会者还包括众议院议长迈克·约翰逊和副总统万斯等高官，他们认为正式的安全措施会损害美国的竞争力。 In the middle of it all was Mr. Trump, who has punted to a group of executives to decide how best to wrangle the rapidly evolving technology, or whether it should be wrangled at all. 处于中心位置的是特朗普，他把决定如何最好地管控这项快速发展的技术，甚至是否应该对其进行管控的问题，推给了一群高管。 “There’s going to be a tremendous self-policing aspect,” Mr. Trump said. “将会包含大量自我监管的成分，”特朗普说。 The one-page document is short on details and relies on the companies to follow through with their promises. It is not an official order, and it is unclear who would enforce the guidance. It was signed by Mr. Trump and the leaders of Anthropic, Google, Meta, Nvidia, OpenAI and SpaceXAI. 这份只有一页纸的文件缺乏细节，主要依赖于各公司履行其承诺。它不是一项官方命令，也不清楚谁将强制执行该指导方针。它由特朗普以及Anthropic、谷歌、Meta、英伟达、OpenAI和SpaceXAI的领导人共同签署。 The agreement echoes voluntary safety commitments by A.I. companies made during the Biden administration. The companies agreed to test their systems for safety and to report safety and security incidents. But the commitments were nonbinding and largely lost at the start of the Trump administration, when the president rolled back safety requirements. 该协议呼应了拜登政府期间人工智能公司做出的自愿安全承诺。这些公司当时同意测试其系统的安全性，并报告安全和安保事件。但这些承诺是不具约束力的，并在特朗普政府初期基本失效，当时总统撤销了安全要求。 The business leaders invited to the White House on Tuesday included Dario Amodei, the chief executive of Anthropic, who has called for federal safety regulations, including the testing of models. Earlier this month, Mr. Amodei called for an industrywide slowdown of A.I. development, citing safety concerns. 周二受邀前往白宫的商界领袖包括Anthropic的首席执行官达里奥·阿莫代伊，他曾呼吁制定联邦安全法规，包括对模型进行测试。本月早些时候，阿莫代伊以安全担忧为由，呼吁整个行业放缓人工智能的发展。 The company has also been embroiled in a legal fight with the administration, and has been barred from working with the Pentagon. The two sides disagreed in negotiations over a $200 million contract, with the company’s insisting that its A.I. technology not be used in mass surveillance of Americans or for autonomous lethal weapons. Speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Mr. Trump called Mr. Amodei “fantastic.” 该公司还卷入了与政府的法律纠纷，并被禁止与五角大楼合作。双方在一项价值2亿美元的合同谈判中存在分歧，该公司坚持要求其人工智能技术不得用于对美国人的大规模监控或用于自主致命武器。周二对记者讲话时，特朗普称阿莫代伊“非常出色”。 Also on the guest list was Jensen Huang, the chief executive of Nvidia and a close Trump ally, who has called the safety concerns exaggerated. Mr. Huang has implored the administration and lawmakers to keep a hands-off approach to regulating the industry, saying rules would allow rival China to speed past the United States on A.I. leadership. 出席嘉宾名单中还有英伟达首席执行官、特朗普的亲密盟友黄仁勋，他曾称这些安全担忧被夸大了。黄仁勋曾恳求政府和立法者对该行业的监管保持不干涉态度，称相关规则将使竞争对手中国在人工智能领导地位上迅速超越美国。 When the group appeared with reporters, the president called Mr. Huang a “very handsome guy” and asked him to speak. 当这群人与记者见面时，总统称黄仁勋是个“非常英俊的家伙”，并请他发言。 “We’re going to advance this technology that is so consequential to humanity, so consequential to the future prosperity of our nation,” Mr. Huang told reporters. “We’re going to do it responsibly and safely.” “我们将推进这项对人类如此重要、对我们国家未来繁荣都非常重要的技术，”黄仁勋告诉记者。“我们将以负责任且安全的方式推进这项工作。” Others invited to the luncheon included Jeff Bezos, the founder of Amazon; Greg Brockman, the president of OpenAI; Alex Karp, the chief executive of Palantir; Sundar Pichai of Google; Mark Zuckerberg of Meta; and Elon Musk of SpaceXAI. The White House chief of staff, Susie Wiles, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent were there. David Sacks, Mr. Trump’s former top adviser on A.I. and a venture capitalist, also attended. 受邀参加午餐会的人士还包括亚马逊创始人杰夫·贝佐斯；OpenAI总裁格雷格·布罗克曼；Palantir首席执行官亚历克斯·卡普；谷歌的桑达尔·皮查伊；Meta的马克·扎克伯格；以及SpaceXAI的埃隆·马斯克。白宫办公厅主任苏西·威尔斯和财政部长斯科特·贝森特也在场。特朗普的前首席人工智能顾问、风险投资家戴维·萨克斯也出席了会议。 Before the luncheon, Mr. Trump told the audience at an event unveiling America.gov, an A.I.-powered search tool, that the U.S. government was championing the technology in an effort to counter China, a major rival in the race to develop A.I. 在午餐会之前，特朗普在人工智能驱动搜索工具America.gov的发布活动上告诉听众，美国政府正在拥护这项技术，努力抗衡人工智能发展竞赛中的主要对手中国。 “We don’t want to stifle growth,” the president said. “我们不想扼杀增长，”总统说。 Mr. Trump, who hosted a state visit last week for Xi Jinping, the Chinese leader, said that the two did not spend much time discussing opportunities for partnerships or issues related to competition. Mr. Xi said in remarks at the White House that both nations shared the responsibility to develop A.I. with “the well-being of the people” in mind. 上周刚刚接待中国领导人习近平进行国事访问的特朗普表示，两人并没有花太多时间讨论合作机会或与竞争相关的议题。习近平在白宫发表讲话时表示，两国在发展人工智能时，都应以“造福于民”为出发点，并肩承担起这一责任。 But in front of a crowd of executives and cabinet members, who were gathered in an auditorium for a presentation that took on the veneer of an Apple product-launch event, the president reiterated a winner-take-all mentality. 但在众多高管和内阁成员面前——他们聚集在礼堂里，举行一场如同苹果新品发布会般的演讲——总统再次重申了赢家通吃的思维方式。 “You’re going to have a winner, or you’re going to have a loser,” Mr. Trump said. “你要么成为赢家，要么成为输家，”特朗普说。 特朗普推动美国在人工智能领域寻求对中国的优势。 Mr. Trump has argued that American dominance over A.I. technology is imperative for national security and economic growth. 特朗普一直主张，美国在人工智能技术上的主导地位对国家安全和经济增长至关重要。 With his embrace of A.I. and support for the development of data centers throughout the country, Mr. Trump is also increasingly out of step with the public. Recent polling shows that a majority of Americans are growing more concerned about A.I. and want the federal government to do more to regulate the technology. 随着他大力拥抱人工智能并支持在全国范围内建设数据中心，特朗普的步调也同公众愈发不一。近期的民意调查显示，多数美国人对人工智能日益担忧，并希望联邦政府采取更多措施来监管这项技术。 On Tuesday, Mr. Trump again came down on the side of data centers, calling concerns about them a Democratic hoax. Flanked by executives at the luncheon, Mr. Trump predicted that the public would eventually embrace the facilities. 周二，特朗普再次为数据中心发声，称对数据中心的担忧是民主党的骗局。午餐会上，在企业高管们的簇拥下，特朗普预测公众最终会接受这些设施。 “You’re going to see data centers are going to be very popular, because this is the group, and they’re the ones that want to, and they’re also the ones that want to see communities that are safe and happy,” Mr. Trump said. “Otherwise, they’ll be forced to go overseas or other locations.” “你们会看到数据中心将变得非常受欢迎，因为这就是那群人，他们是想要建设这些中心的人，他们也是希望看到社区安全和快乐的人，”特朗普说。“否则，这些数据中心将被迫迁往海外或其他地方。” 特朗普与包括Meta、英伟达、SpaceXAI和谷歌在内的主要科技公司领导人合影。 As the public has soured on A.I. and the prospect of data centers mushrooming around the country, the debate over technology safety has intensified in recent weeks. Several rogue A.I. clients and models have worked together to breach websites, steal data and then cover their tracks, all while appearing to show an understanding that what they were doing was wrong. Senior leaders in Congress have acknowledged the need for A.I. safety guardrails. 随着公众对人工智能以及数据中心在全国各地如雨后春笋般涌现的前景感到反感，近几周来，关于技术安全的辩论愈发激烈。一些失控的人工智能客户端和模型曾协同入侵网站、窃取数据，然后掩盖其踪迹，而在此过程中，它们似乎还表现出对自身行为错误性的认知。国会的高层领导人已经承认了设置人工智能安全护栏的必要性。 In April, Anthropic announced it was holding back the release of one of its models, Mythos, because it was too dangerous for the public. In July, OpenAI models broke out of a restricted testing environment and hacked the A.I. start-up Hugging Face. In early September, leaders of Anthropic, OpenAI and Google DeepMind called for slowing development of advanced A.I. models. 今年4月，Anthropic宣布暂停发布其一个名为Mythos的模型，理由是该模型对公众而言过于危险。今年7月，OpenAI的模型突破了受限的测试环境，入侵了人工智能初创公司Hugging Face。在9月初，Anthropic、OpenAI和谷歌DeepMind的领导人们呼吁放缓高级人工智能模型的开发。 Last week, an OpenAI model was found to have meddled with U.S. government websites including the Education Department, the Securities and Exchange Commission and Commerce Department’s census site. And this week, OpenAI said it would not release its latest model, GPT-6.1 Astra, over safety concerns. 上周，一个OpenAI模型被发现干扰了包括美国教育部、证券交易委员会以及商务部人口普查网站在内的美国政府网站。而本周，OpenAI表示出于安全考虑，将不会发布其最新模型GPT-6.1 Astra。 Within the White House, senior leaders are at odds on how to regulate the industry. Mr. Bessent has floated the idea of an open dialogue with China on safety standards. He has also stressed that A.I. companies must be held accountable for harms created by their models. 在白宫内部，高层领导人对如何监管该行业存在分歧。贝森特提出了就安全标准与中国进行公开对话的想法。他还强调，人工智能公司必须为其模型造成的危害承担责任。 Meta总裁兼副主席迪娜·鲍威尔·麦考密克（中）周二出席了此次活动。 As his day with the billionaires wrapped up on Tuesday, Mr. Trump said that he was considering a committee of about 10 people focused on A.I. safety, and that he would name an A.I. czar in the coming days. 随着周二与亿万富翁们共度的一天走向结束，特朗普表示，他正在考虑成立一个由大约10人组成、专门负责人工智能安全的委员会，并且他将在未来几天内任命一位人工智能领域的事务专员。 He ended his final appearance with reporters alongside Mr. Musk, another attendee who has worked himself back into Mr. Trump’s good graces after a spat last year over domestic policy legislation. He was seated near Mr. Xi and Mr. Trump at last week’s state dinner, and was at Mr. Trump’s side at the luncheon on Tuesday. 当天他最后一次面见记者时，陪伴在他身边的是马斯克。马斯克也是与会者，在去年因国内政策立法发生口角后，如今已重新赢得了特朗普的青睐。在上周的国宴上，他坐在习近平和特朗普附近，在周二的午餐会上，他也坐在特朗普身边。 Mr. Xi, the president said, “will take every data center that we don’t want.” 总统说，习近平“会接手所有我们不想要的数据中心。” Standing nearby, Mr. Musk agreed. 站在旁边的马斯克表示同意。 “He would love that, every single one, because you know why? They’re smart,” Mr. Trump continued. “They want every data center. They want it because that’s great for China. Well, it’s great for us, and we’re leading by a lot, and we're going to keep it that way.” “他会很乐意的，每一个都要，因为你知道为什么吗？他们很聪明，”特朗普继续说道。“他们想要每一个数据中心。他们想要是因为这对中国大有好处。好吧，这对我们也很有好处，而且我们遥遥领先，我们会继续保持这种优势。” Kalley Huang contributed reporting. Katie Rogers是《纽约时报》白宫记者，报道特朗普总统相关新闻。 Cecilia Kang自华盛顿为《纽约时报》报道科技和监管政策。她撰写有关科技的报道已超过20年。 翻译：晋其角 点击查看本文英文版。
content: KATIE ROGERS, CECILIA KANG 2026年9月30日 周二，特朗普总统在白宫向公众推出一个由人工智能驱动的政府网站。 Doug Mills/The New York Times President Trump summoned the world’s most powerful technology executives to the White House on Tuesday, and praised the assembled billionaires as “very brilliant” minds who wanted to make the world a better place through job creation, the construction of data centers and the rapid expansion of artificial intelligence. 特朗普总统周二将全球最有权势的科技高管召集到白宫，称赞与会的亿万富翁们是“非常杰出”的人才，称他们希望通过创造就业机会、建设数据中心以及快速扩张人工智能让世界变得更美好。 As president, Mr. Trump faces questions about whether A.I. should be regulated, and particularly whether restrictions should be put in place to protect humans from technology that has learned to outmaneuver existing safeguards. 作为总统，特朗普面临着人工智能是否应该受到监管的质询，特别是是否应该实施限制措施，避免人类受到已学会规避现有安全防护措施的技术的伤害。 But in the end, convening all of those billions and all of that brain power did not result in a commitment to formal regulation. Instead, they signed a voluntary agreement to adopt safety policies that include risk reviews, auditing and evaluations of systems by third parties. They also agreed to adopt Mr. Trump’s preferred rebranding of A.I.: “super intelligence.” 但最终，召集这些亿万富翁和顶尖大脑并没有带来对正式监管的承诺。取而代之的是，他们签署了一项 自愿协议 ，承诺采取安全政策，包括由第三方对系统进行风险审查、审计和评估。他们还同意采用特朗普偏爱的人工智能新名称：“超级智能”。 “This is going to be all for the good, and we’re going to have it be nice and safe,” Mr. Trump said on Tuesday afternoon, when he and the tech leaders took questions outside the White House. “And they’re really going to be policing each other, and that’s the way it works.” “这一切都将是为了更好的未来，我们将让它变得美好且安全，”特朗普在周二下午与科技领袖们在白宫外接受提问时说道。“而且他们真的会互相监督，这就是它的运作方式。” Asked if the agreement would be binding, Mr. Trump said, “I think it’s morally binding.” 当被问及该协议是否具有约束力时，特朗普说：“我认为它具有道德约束力。” Inside the White House luncheon, Mr. Trump’s seating chart (which he posted on social media) revealed a powerful assemblage of executives who are deeply divided on the need for A.I. safeguards. The meeting also included top officials, such as Speaker Mike Johnson and Vice President JD Vance, who believe that formalized safeguards would hurt American competitiveness. 在白宫午餐会上，特朗普公布的座位表（由他本人发布在社交媒体上）显示，与会的高管们实力雄厚，但在是否需要制定人工智能保障措施的问题上存在严重分歧。与会者还包括众议院议长迈克·约翰逊和副总统万斯等高官，他们认为正式的安全措施会损害美国的竞争力。 In the middle of it all was Mr. Trump, who has punted to a group of executives to decide how best to wrangle the rapidly evolving technology, or whether it should be wrangled at all. 处于中心位置的是特朗普，他把决定如何最好地管控这项快速发展的技术，甚至是否应该对其进行管控的问题，推给了一群高管。 “There’s going to be a tremendous self-policing aspect,” Mr. Trump said. “将会包含大量自我监管的成分，”特朗普说。 The one-page document is short on details and relies on the companies to follow through with their promises. It is not an official order, and it is unclear who would enforce the guidance. It was signed by Mr. Trump and the leaders of Anthropic, Google, Meta, Nvidia, OpenAI and SpaceXAI. 这份只有一页纸的文件缺乏细节，主要依赖于各公司履行其承诺。它不是一项官方命令，也不清楚谁将强制执行该指导方针。它由特朗普以及Anthropic、谷歌、Meta、英伟达、OpenAI和SpaceXAI的领导人共同签署。 The agreement echoes voluntary safety commitments by A.I. companies made during the Biden administration. The companies agreed to test their systems for safety and to report safety and security incidents. But the commitments were nonbinding and largely lost at the start of the Trump administration, when the president rolled back safety requirements. 该协议呼应了拜登政府期间人工智能公司做出的自愿安全承诺。这些公司当时同意测试其系统的安全性，并报告安全和安保事件。但这些承诺是不具约束力的，并在特朗普政府初期基本失效，当时总统撤销了安全要求。 The business leaders invited to the White House on Tuesday included Dario Amodei , the chief executive of Anthropic, who has called for federal safety regulations, including the testing of models. Earlier this month, Mr. Amodei called for an industrywide slowdown of A.I. development, citing safety concerns. 周二受邀前往白宫的商界领袖包括Anthropic的首席执行官 达里奥·阿莫代伊 ，他曾呼吁制定联邦安全法规，包括对模型进行测试。本月早些时候，阿莫代伊以安全担忧为由，呼吁整个行业放缓人工智能的发展。 The company has also been embroiled in a legal fight with the administration, and has been barred from working with the Pentagon . The two sides disagreed in negotiations over a $200 million contract, with the company’s insisting that its A.I. technology not be used in mass surveillance of Americans or for autonomous lethal weapons. He has also stressed that A.I. companies must be held accountable for harms created by their models. 在白宫内部，高层领导人对如何监管该行业存在分歧。贝森特提出了就安全标准与中国进行公开对话的想法。他还强调，人工智能公司必须为其模型造成的危害承担责任。 Meta总裁兼副主席迪娜·鲍威尔·麦考密克（中）周二出席了此次活动。 As his day with the billionaires wrapped up on Tuesday, Mr. Trump said that he was considering a committee of about 10 people focused on A.I. safety, and that he would name an A.I. czar in the coming days. 随着周二与亿万富翁们共度的一天走向结束，特朗普表示，他正在考虑成立一个由大约10人组成、专门负责人工智能安全的委员会，并且他将在未来几天内任命一位人工智能领域的事务专员。 He ended his final appearance with reporters alongside Mr. Musk, another attendee who has worked himself back into Mr. Trump’s good graces after a spat last year over domestic policy legislation. He was seated near Mr. Xi and Mr. Trump at last week’s state dinner, and was at Mr. Trump’s side at the luncheon on Tuesday. 当天他最后一次面见记者时，陪伴在他身边的是马斯克。马斯克也是与会者，在去年因国内政策立法发生口角后，如今已重新赢得了特朗普的青睐。在上周的国宴上，他坐在习近平和特朗普附近，在周二的午餐会上，他也坐在特朗普身边。 Mr. Xi, the president said, “will take every data center that we don’t want.” 总统说，习近平“会接手所有我们不想要的数据中心。” Standing nearby, Mr. Musk agreed. 站在旁边的马斯克表示同意。 “He would love that, every single one, because you know why? They’re smart,” Mr. Trump continued. “They want every data center. They want it because that’s great for China. Well, it’s great for us, and we’re leading by a lot, and we're going to keep it that way.” “他会很乐意的，每一个都要，因为你知道为什么吗？他们很聪明，”特朗普继续说道。“他们想要每一个数据中心。他们想要是因为这对中国大有好处。好吧，这对我们也很有好处，而且我们遥遥领先，我们会继续保持这种优势。” Kalley Huang contributed reporting. Katie Rogers 是《纽约时报》白宫记者，报道特朗普总统相关新闻。 Cecilia Kang 自华盛顿为《纽约时报》报道科技和监管政策。她撰写有关科技的报道已超过20年。 翻译：晋其角 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 一名锡安教会被捕牧师妻子的流亡、煎熬与信仰
description: 王月眉2026年9月29日耿朋朋在住处的前院。 On the 308th day after the Chinese police took her husband, Cherie Geng was making dumplings. The smell of a finished batch wafted from the kitchen as she mixed flour and water at her dining table. Her 6-year-old son was busy trading Pokemon figurines with a friend, so Cherie pushed a plate toward the friend’s mom, who had come to drop him off for the play date. 在中国警方带走她丈夫后的第308天，耿朋朋正在包饺子。她在餐桌上和面时，厨房里飘来一阵刚出锅的饺子的香味。她六岁的儿子正忙着和一个小伙伴交换宝可梦玩偶，于是耿朋朋把一盘饺子推向那位小朋友的妈妈——她是送孩子过来玩的。 “This is pretty good — the dough is soft,” the other mom said. “Last time I made dough, it was so hard I felt like I was choking.” “这个挺好吃的——面很软，”那位妈妈说。“我上次和的面特别硬，吃得我都觉得噎得慌。” “I’m not great at it either,” Cherie said. “Normally it’s my husband who likes making dumplings.” He had been a one-man assembly line, sifting flour, mixing filling and folding wrappers. “If we were feeding two or three people, he’d say, ‘You don’t need to do anything.’” “我也不太会，”耿朋朋说道，“平时都是我丈夫喜欢包饺子。”以前，他包起饺子来就像一条一个人的流水线，从筛面粉、拌馅到包饺子，全都不在话下。“要是只做两三个人吃的，他就会说，‘你什么都不用干。’” Now, though, Cherie had to do everything. Her husband, a pastor at one of China’s biggest underground churches, was seized last October by officers who roused him from bed at 2 a.m. Afterward, Cherie, fearing arrest herself, had fled with their son to Thailand. Since then, she had been in charge of not just cooking, but also renting a home, sorting out visas, finding schools and earning an income. She’d had to figure out where she could find authentic Chinese beef noodles, where to buy Chinese picture books. Having just learned to drive in Beijing, she now had to drive on the other side of the road. 可现在，什么都得耿朋朋自己来。她的丈夫是中国规模最大的地下教会之一的一名牧师，去年10月的一天，警察在凌晨2点把他从睡梦中叫醒并带走。之后，耿朋朋担心自己也会被捕，于是带着儿子逃到泰国。从那以后，她不仅要做饭，还得租房、办签证、找学校、挣钱养家。她得弄清楚哪里能吃到正宗的中国牛肉面，哪里可以买到中文绘本。她刚在北京学会开车，现在却得适应靠左行驶。 All this while trying to get her husband out of jail. She spent hours learning the intricacies of Chinese law and trying to craft attention-grabbing social media posts. Most days, it felt like all she could do was explain to her son where his father was. 与此同时，她还得设法营救丈夫出狱。她花了很多时间钻研中国法律的种种细节，还要琢磨怎样写出能引起关注的社交媒体帖子。大多数日子里，她觉得自己能做的只有向儿子解释爸爸去了哪里。 耿朋朋的丈夫高颖佳是中国最大地下教会之一的二号人物。当耿朋朋带着六岁的儿子约翰逃到泰国时，约翰不太会说英语，在课堂上有些吃力。 The Chinese government’s crackdown on Zion Church was its biggest roundup of Christians in nearly a decade, as the authorities have increasingly tried to shut down religious groups that do not declare loyalty to the ruling Communist Party. In May, President Trump personally asked China’s leader, Xi Jinping, to free the lead pastor, Ezra Jin; Jin was soon released and now lives in the United States. 中国政府对锡安教会的打压是近十年来针对基督徒规模最大的一次集中抓捕。近年来，当局越来越严厉地打压那些不愿向执政的共产党宣示效忠的宗教团体。今年5月，特朗普总统亲自请求中国领导人习近平释放锡安教会主任牧师金明日；不久后，金明日获释，现在生活在美国。 But eight church members remain in detention, including Cherie’s husband, Gao Yingjia. China has signaled that it may sentence them to more than 10 years in prison, and their families are desperately trying to keep attention on their cases. 但仍有八名教会成员遭到羁押，其中包括耿朋朋的丈夫高颖佳。中国已经释放信号，他们可能会被判处十年以上有期徒刑，而他们的家人正拼命让外界持续关注这些案件。 At the same time, they must contend with how the arrests have rippled through their own lives. Most of the relatives who remain free had little public role at the church, and little preparation for what befell them. When Cherie once asked her husband whether they should make a plan in case he was arrested, he replied that they should just place their faith in God. 与此同时，他们还不得不应付亲人被抓给自己的生活带来的连锁冲击。这些仍然自由的家属大多过去在教会里并不担任什么公开角色，对降临在自己身上的一切也几乎毫无准备。有一次，耿朋朋问丈夫，万一他被捕，他们是不是应该提前做个打算。丈夫回答说，他们只需要信靠上帝。 Now, Cherie, 46, had little choice. It wasn’t easy. She was on her own in a part of Thailand she had never been to before, unsure when she might see her home or her husband again. Even here, she didn’t feel totally safe: She slept with a golf club by her bed and didn’t want her specific location published, in case the Chinese police tried to track her down. Her husband’s trial had recently been postponed without explanation, which gave her faint hope that the charges would be dropped and he would be freed. But Cherie also knew that outcome was most likely preordained, and the delay might just mean more time in limbo. 如今，46岁的耿朋朋几乎没有选择。这并不容易。她独自生活在泰国一个以前从未去过的地方，不知道什么时候才能再见到自己的家，也不知道什么时候才能再见到丈夫。即使到了这里，她也不觉得完全安全：睡觉时，她会在床边放一根高尔夫球杆，也不希望报道披露她的具体住处，担心中国警方会设法追踪到她。丈夫的庭审不久前无故延期，这让她燃起了一丝微弱的希望——或许指控会被撤销，他会重获自由。但耿朋朋也明白，结果很可能早已注定，延期或许只意味着这段悬而未决的日子还要继续。 In her hardest moments, Cherie allowed herself to imagine how things might have been different. Before she became a mother and a pastor’s wife, she had earned a Ph.D. in genetics and held a lucrative job at a pharmaceutical company. She could picture a world in which she had never become a Christian, never married a pastor and just lived a comfortable life. 在最艰难的时刻，耿朋朋也会放任自己去想像，如果当初不一样，现在会怎样。在成为母亲和牧师妻子之前，她拿到了遗传学博士学位，并在一家制药公司拥有一份高薪工作。她能在脑海中描绘出另一种人生：自己从未成为基督徒，从未嫁给牧师，只是过着安逸的生活。 为了防身，耿朋朋睡觉时会在床边放一根高尔夫球杆。她儿子常做噩梦，梦见妈妈被抓走。 耿朋朋和约翰在一位朋友陪同下出门去教会。 Still, in some ways her ordeal had made her feel closer to her faith, and her husband, than ever before. Between batches of dumplings, she shared a post on X calling for the pastors’ freedom, and sent a text message to the other pastors’ relatives to confirm a strategy call later that night. Whenever she had time, she typed notes into her phone, both for herself and to write in letters for her husband, even though the jail rarely let mail in or out. 不过，从某些方面说，这场磨难反而让她觉得自己比以往任何时候都更贴近自己的信仰，也更贴近丈夫。包饺子的间隙，她在X平台上转发了一篇呼吁释放牧师们的帖子，又给其他被捕牧师的家属发短信，确认当晚晚些时候商议对策的通话。只要有一点时间，她就会在手机里记下些东西，有些是写给自己看的，有些则准备写进给丈夫的信里，尽管监狱通信受到严格限制。 “Dear Yingjia, I miss you,” she began. “亲爱的颖佳，我想你了，”她写道。 *** *** Relatives of the detainees logged onto the video call from all over the world: a wife who had fled to California, a husband in South Korea, elderly parents inside China. Sitting at her dining table, which was still cluttered with mixing bowls and her son’s toys, Cherie greeted the other church members’ loved ones, 12 in all, on her phone screen. 被关押的教会成员的亲属从世界各地接入视频通话：一名逃到加州的妻子、一名身在韩国的丈夫，还有仍在中国境内的年迈父母。耿朋朋坐在餐桌旁，桌上散落着和面的碗和儿子的玩具。她看着手机屏幕，向其他教会成员的亲人打招呼，一共有12个人。 “Thanks for all your work today,” she said to the father of a pastor who had spent the day writing letters of protest to government officials. “今天辛苦你了，”她对一位牧师的父亲说。那位父亲花了一整天时间给政府官员写抗议信。 “You haven’t been feeling well lately, right?” she said to another pastor’s husband. “Do you think you have Covid?” “你最近一直不太舒服，对吧？”她对另一位牧师的丈夫说。“是不是得了新冠？” They hadn’t been close before the arrests. Zion Church’s leaders had been scattered across China for years, since the government barred them from gathering in Beijing. The pastors led smaller, low-profile groups instead, coming together on Sundays for sermons streamed on Zoom, many of them given by Cherie’s husband, the church’s second-in-command. 在抓捕发生之前，他们彼此并不亲近。自从政府禁止锡安教会在北京聚会后，教会的领袖多年来一直分散在中国各地。牧师们转而带领规模更小、行事更低调的聚会，每逢星期日再通过Zoom一起听讲道，其中许多次讲道都是耿朋朋的丈夫主持的，他是锡安教会的二号带领人。 Thousands of people tuned in. The church leaders knew that the police were likely among them, but they believed it was their duty to spread the gospel proudly and fearlessly. Besides, the authorities generally hadn’t imprisoned church leaders as long as they did not directly challenge the government. Yingjia and others had been hauled in for questioning and even held for a few days, but they were always released afterward. 每次都有数千人上线收看。教会领袖们知道，警察很可能也混在其中，但他们相信，自豪而无所畏惧地传播福音是自己的责任。况且，只要不直接挑战政府，当局通常不会长期监禁教会领袖。高颖佳和其他人过去都曾被带走问话，甚至拘留过几天，但最后总会放回来。 Growing up in the countryside of northern China, Cherie had been introduced to Christianity by her mother, who hid with fellow worshipers in pig stalls to secretly listen to a local pastor. Her mother discouraged Cherie from joining a church herself, worrying that it was dangerous. But Cherie found her own way to faith when her work at the pharmaceutical company left her feeling empty. Bubbly, sociable and fluent in English after her Ph.D. studies, she left her job and started teaching the language to fellow churchgoers. 耿朋朋在中国北方农村长大，是母亲把她引入基督教信仰的。她的母亲曾经和其他教友躲在猪圈里，偷偷听一位当地牧师讲道。母亲劝耿朋朋自己不要加入教会，担心那样太危险。但后来，在制药公司的工作让耿朋朋感到内心空虚，她最终还是以自己的方式走向了信仰。她性格开朗、善于交际，攻读博士期间练就了一口流利英语。后来她辞掉工作，开始给教会里的其他信徒教英语。 Still, worry was never far from her mind, especially after she and Yingjia adopted their son, John, in 2021. Her health was also deteriorating — maybe, she thought, because of the stress of frequent police raids on church meetings. Last summer, rumors began spreading that a bigger crackdown might be coming. 尽管如此，心里总还是担心，尤其是在她和高颖佳2021年收养儿子约翰之后。她的身体也开始变差了——她猜想，也许是因为警方经常突袭教会聚会带来的压力。去年夏天，开始有传言说，一场更大规模的打压可能即将到来。 It came on Oct. 10, when they were at home in Beijing. Cherie received a call from a lawyer who said Zion’s lead pastor had been arrested, along with around two dozen other church members. 10月10日，这场打压真的来了。当时他们正在北京家中。耿朋朋接到一名律师的电话，对方告诉她，锡安教会的主任牧师已经被捕，此外还有大约二十多名教会成员也被带走。 Scrambling, they removed their SIM cards from their phones and drove with their son to a friend’s house. But the police pounded on their friend’s door in the middle of the night and took Yingjia away. They accused him of illegal use of the internet in connection with his online sermons. 他们慌忙取出手机里的电话卡，带着儿子开车去了一个朋友家。但半夜，警察猛敲朋友家的门，把高颖佳带走了。他们指控他非法利用信息网络，这与他线上讲道有关。 Cherie returned home to find her door broken open, her apartment stripped of electronics, books and her diaries. In the following days, she vomited repeatedly. Why hadn’t Yingjia wanted to make a plan? What was she supposed to do now? 耿朋朋回到家时，发现家门已被撬开，公寓里的电子设备、书籍和她的日记都被搜走了。接下来的几天里，她反复呕吐。为什么颖佳不肯提前做个计划？她现在该怎么办？ At first, she resolved to stay in China. The police wouldn’t let her see her husband, but she could see his lawyers, who were allowed to visit him. She told John that his father was on a long business trip. But John overheard her talking to the lawyers and started having nightmares about her being seized, too. 起初，她决心留在中国。警方不让她见丈夫，但她可以见他的律师，而律师获准前去探视。她告诉约翰，父亲在长期出差。但约翰偷听到她和律师的谈话，开始做噩梦，梦见她也被抓走。 She arrived in Thailand in January. It was a shock in many ways: the humidity, the noisy streets. She found an English-speaking congregation, and at first she marveled that she could worship without fear of persecution. But she also missed the sense of urgency that had come with Zion’s furtive services in China. The new pastor’s sermons, on comfortable domestic topics like parenting and education, sometimes felt distant from her own concerns. 今年1月，她来到泰国。很多东西都让她很不适应：湿热的天气、嘈杂的街道。她找到了一间使用英语的教会，起初，她惊叹于自己竟然可以不用担心遭受迫害，自由地做礼拜。可她同时也怀念起锡安教会在中国偷偷举行礼拜时那种紧迫感。新教会牧师的讲道谈的常常是育儿、教育之类安稳日常生活中的话题，有时让她觉得离自己的处境相距甚远。 She hesitated to tell people she met about her situation, not wanting pity or unsolicited advice. The sight of couples and families pained her. A few other Zion members had also fled to Thailand, but Cherie often wanted to be alone. She purposely chose a house way too big for just herself and John so she had a space to withdraw. 因为不想要同情，也不想听别人主动给她建议，所以她不太愿意向新认识的人讲述自己的遭遇。看到夫妻和一家人在一起，会让她感到难过。另有几名锡安教会成员也逃到了泰国，但耿朋朋常常只想一个人待着。她特意租了一栋对于她和约翰两个人来说大得过分的房子，这样她便能有一个可以独处的空间。 Every night, she and John prayed together in their bedroom facing a yard with mango and papaya trees. He always prayed to go back to Beijing. 每天晚上，她都会和约翰一起在卧室里祷告。卧室外是一片院子，种着芒果和木瓜。他总是祷告希望能回北京。 一开始，耿朋朋对约翰说爸爸出差了，但如今他已经知道，爸爸被关在监狱里。但想到爸爸在监狱里仍在向人传道，他反倒从中得到了一些安慰。中国宪法保障宗教信仰自由。但在实际执行中，政府只允许经官方批准、并宣示效忠中共的宗教团体开展活动。 Now she was at a rented dining table, collecting morsels about her husband’s case in the only way she could: through calls with the families of other detainees. Recently, as the trial loomed, the meetings had become more frequent. Cherie now knew the other relatives’ morning and evening routines, their parents’ names, their deepest fears. 如今，她坐在一张租来的餐桌旁，只能通过和其他被羁押者家属通话，一点一点拼凑出丈夫案件的消息。最近，随着开庭日期临近，这样的会议变得越来越频繁。现在，耿朋朋已经知道其他家属的早晚作息，知道他们父母的名字，也知道他们心底最深的恐惧。 The woman who had fled to California sounded tired as she joined the conversation — it was 5 a.m. there. Her voice shaky, she said the prosecutors were threatening her husband with a decadelong sentence if he didn’t plead guilty. 逃到加州的那名女子加入通话时听起来十分疲惫——她那边才清晨5点。她声音颤抖地说，检察官正在威胁她的丈夫：如果不认罪，就判他十年。 “Could that be a trap?” one father interjected. “会不会是在诈他？”一位父亲插话说。 “I think we need to ask the lawyers again what’s going on,” Cherie said. She often found herself in the role of mediator and comforter, her old teaching instincts kicking in. “If anyone else’s lawyers can go, too, they should try to find out if they’re increasing the pressure.” “我觉得我们得再问问律师，到底是怎么回事，”耿朋朋说。她常常发现自己扮演着调解者和安慰者的角色，过去教书时养成的习惯又冒了出来。“如果其他人的律师也能去，他们应该尽量问清楚，他们是不是在加大施压。” “Sometimes they just exaggerate,” another caller said. “They might only plan to sentence you to three years, but they say 11.” “他们有时候就是故意往严重了说，”另一名通话者说。“也许本来只打算判你三年，却会跟你说要判11年。” The conversation turned to when the court might reschedule the trial, when John, who had been playing on a tablet in the next room, started shouting. 大家的话题转到法院可能什么时候重新安排庭审。这时，一直在隔壁房间玩平板电脑的约翰突然大声喊了起来。 “Mom! What’s wrong with this?” When she didn’t answer, he called again. “Mom, what’s wrong with this?” “妈妈！这个怎么回事？”她没有回答，于是他又喊了一遍。“妈妈，这个怎么回事？” She knew that John didn’t like it when she was glued to her phone. Rarely fussy in Beijing, he had become irritable since his father’s arrest. He got into fights at school and called Cherie ugly. She, in turn, sometimes yelled at or spanked him, and always regretted doing so afterward. 她知道，约翰不喜欢她总是盯着手机。在北京时他很少闹脾气，但自从父亲被抓后，他变得易怒。他会在学校里和人打架，还会骂耿朋朋丑。耿朋朋有时也会反过来冲他大喊，或者打他屁股，事后又总是后悔。 Cherie set her phone on the table and walked over. “It’s out of battery,” she said. 耿朋朋把手机放在桌上，走了过去。“是没电了，”她说。 “Mom, come with me,” he said, tugging her toward the stairs. “妈妈，跟我来，”他说着，拉着她往楼梯那边走。 “You go ahead,” she said, trying to dislodge him gently. But he wouldn’t relent, so she followed him. “你自己去吧，”她说，试着轻轻挣脱他。但他不肯放手，于是她跟着他去了。 几个月来，约翰每天晚上都会祈祷，希望能够回到北京。耿朋朋每周会和其他教会成员的家属或高颖佳的律师通话数次。如今，她与人交往主要都靠手机。 She returned to the dining room a few minutes later, looking weary. She unmuted herself and put on a cheery voice. 几分钟后，她回到餐厅，看起来满脸疲惫。她取消静音，装出轻快的声音。 “What’s going on now?” she said. “现在说到哪儿了？”她问。 *** *** When Cherie and Yingjia first met through Zion, she thought he was too short, too serious and chewed too loudly. Like her, he had done a Ph.D. — his was in theoretical physics — but unlike her, he fulfilled the stereotype of the awkward scientist. But Cherie’s mother kept pressuring her to find a husband, and there weren’t many bachelors at Zion. Cherie decided to think of her marriage as a sacrifice to Christ. 耿朋朋和高颖佳最初在锡安教会认识时，她觉得他个子太矮、太严肃，吃东西时声音太大。和她一样，他也有博士学位——他的专业是理论物理，但和她不同的是，他完全符合人们对科学家都是书呆子的刻板印象。可耿朋朋的母亲一直催她找个丈夫，而锡安教会里单身男人并不多。耿朋朋于是决定，把这段婚姻当作自己为基督作出的牺牲。 Cherie struggled with her new identity as a pastor’s wife. She felt pressure to be good, but she disliked some people at church, lost her temper with Yingjia and still argued with her parents. 成为牧师妻子后，耿朋朋一直不太适应这个新的身份。她感到自己得处处表现得像个好人，可她并不喜欢教会里的某些人，而且她会对高颖佳发脾气，也还是会和父母争吵。 It was Yingjia who told her not to worry, that she should be herself and that God would take care of them. His unflappability drove her crazy at first. But over time, it became part of what she loved about him. 反倒是高颖佳告诉她，不必担心，她只需要做自己，上帝会照顾他们。起初，他这种处变不惊的性格简直让她抓狂。但时间久了，这成了她爱他的原因之一。 Now he wasn’t around, and she felt herself trying to satisfy others’ expectations again. She was always comforting the families of other jailed members; when she got tired, she took it out on John. Yingjia seemed to know that would happen. In one of his few letters that had reached her by mail, he urged her to stop putting on a happy face. “The fact that you always share the good news but not the bad actually makes me a bit sad, because I don’t get to be by your side during the difficult times,” he wrote in a letter dated May 2. 如今他不在身边了，她发现自己又开始努力迎合别人对她的期待。她总是在安慰其他被关押教友的家属；累到撑不住的时候，就会把情绪发泄在约翰身上。高颖佳似乎早就知道她会这样。在少数几封成功寄到她手里的信中，他有劝她不要再强装笑脸。他在5月2日的信中写道：“你总是报喜不报忧，其实反而让我有一点难过，因为你最难熬的时候，我没办法陪在你身边。” She especially felt his absence on June 18. That was the day the court was scheduled to decide whether to move forward with the case against Zion or drop it. Cherie, feeling optimistic, considered booking a flight back home so she could greet Yingjia when he was released. But her friends urged her to wait. 6月18日，她尤其深切地感受到了他的缺席。那天，法院原定裁决是继续审理针对锡安教会的案件还是予以撤销。耿朋朋当时很乐观，考虑订机票回国，这样就能在高颖佳获释时去迎接他。但朋友们劝她再等等。 The morning of the decision, the lawyer called. Some church members had been released on bail, but Yingjia had not. In fact, the court had added charges, describing the offerings Zion had collected as fraud. 裁决当天上午，律师打来电话。一些教会成员已获保释，但高颖佳没有。事实上，法院还追加了指控，把锡安教会募集的奉献定性为欺诈。 Cherie broke down. Friends swarmed her house to comfort her, but she felt only irritation. Why weren’t they offering her more support? Actually, why wouldn’t they go away — how could they know how she was feeling? What if, Cherie wondered, she went back to China, Yingjia gave up pastoring, they found new jobs and just prayed secretly? 耿朋朋崩溃了。朋友们涌到她家安慰她，但她只感到烦躁。为什么他们没有给她更多支持？其实，为什么他们不走开——他们怎么可能了解她的感受？耿朋朋想，如果她回中国，高颖佳放弃牧职，他们各自找个新工作，只然后只在暗中祷告，那会怎么样呢？ *** *** So much of her life now was waiting — for news from the lawyers, for a letter from her husband, for some clarity on what the rest of her life would look like. But there was also so much to deal with every day. That was why, early on the Monday after she made dumplings, Cherie nudged a sleepy John out of bed, for her first day of work. 她现在生活中很大一部分是等待——等待律师的消息，等待丈夫的来信，等待某种关于余生会是什么样子的明确答案。但每天也有太多事情要处理。正因如此，在包完饺子后的那个周一清晨，耿朋朋把睡眼惺忪的约翰从床上推醒，因为这是她第一天上班。 Cherie had hesitated to take a full-time job when she felt she already wasn’t spending enough time with him. But she needed money and a visa. And the job was teaching at a Christian school, so John could attend for free. 耿朋朋曾犹豫要不要接受一份全职工作，因为她觉得自己已经没花足够时间陪他。但她需要钱和签证。而且这份工作是在一所基督教学校教书，所以约翰可以免费上学。 Cherie navigated slowly through morning traffic in the used Toyota Camry she had recently bought. It was a 40-minute drive, and she was still a nervous driver, steering down streets lined with tropical flowers and banana trees. 耿朋朋开着她最近买的一辆二手丰田凯美瑞，缓慢地穿行在早晨的车流中。车程40分钟，她仍然是个紧张的司机，沿着两旁种满热带花卉和香蕉树的街道行驶。 约翰陪着耿朋朋去新工作上班的第一天。耿朋朋开始上泰拳课来增强体力。不过，她答应约翰不会参加比赛，因为约翰担心，万一她受伤了，就没人照顾他了。 “What song do you want to listen to today?” she asked John. “你今天想听什么歌？”她问约翰。 “I don’t want to listen to songs,” he mumbled, his eyes still closed. “我不想听歌，”他嘟囔着，眼睛还闭着。 “Let’s listen to the songs I like then,” she said, putting on a Chinese worship song. “Buckle your seatbelt.” “那就听我喜欢的歌吧，”她说，放了一首中文敬拜歌曲。“系好安全带。” “I don’t have the energy,” he said. “我没力气，”他说。 Lately, Cherie had been returning to one song in particular: “Never Ending Grace.” She had awakened with it playing in her head the morning after her husband wasn’t released on bail. It seemed like a sign, a reminder that everything she was going through had a higher purpose. 最近，耿朋朋总是在听一首歌：《细数恩典》。在她丈夫未能获保释的第二天早上，她醒来时脑海里就回响着这首歌。它像是一个征兆，提醒她，自己所经历的一切都有更高的目的。 Every trial faced where I nearly stumbled 每个险些跌倒路过的试炼 Every day that arrived unnoticed 每个未曾在意到来的今天 Every peaceful moment taken for granted 每个平安无事忽略的瞬间 What seemed ordinary was actually grace 看似理所当然其实是恩典 So she was trying to give herself more grace, too. She had cut back on her meetings with the other families, so she could take John to soccer practice. She went to Muay Thai classes to build up strength (though, she noted in a letter to Yingjia, her abs were still in hiding). She invited her sister to visit from China to help take care of John. 所以她也努力给自己更多恩典。她减少了与其他家庭的聚会，这样就能带约翰去踢足球。她去上泰拳课增强体力。（不过她在给高颖佳的信里提到，她的腹肌仍然没有显露。）她请姐姐从中国来帮忙照顾约翰。 And she prayed, constantly. There was an irony to her situation: Now, when the burden of being a pastor’s wife was heavier than ever, she was finally doing what Yingjia had always advised her to do, just giving up control and trusting in God. 她还不断祷告。她的处境颇具讽刺意味：如今，当身为牧师妻子的重担比以往任何时候都更沉重时，她终于做到了高颖佳一直建议她做的事——放手，信靠上帝。 Cherie sang quietly as she drove. She decided to put the lyrics in her next letter to Yingjia. 耿朋朋一边开车一边轻声唱着。她决定把歌词写进下一封给高颖佳的信里。 *** *** Cherie made it through her first day of work, but she couldn’t rest yet. After a dinner of steamed buns prepared by her sister, Cherie called a family meeting, a tradition from Beijing that had fallen off in the chaos of leaving China. She gathered her sister, her sister’s two children and John around the table to light a candle, sing a hymn and read the Bible. 耿朋朋熬过了第一天上班，但她还不能休息。吃完姐姐准备的蒸馒头做晚餐后，耿朋朋召集了一次家庭会议——这是在北京时的传统，在离开中国的那段混乱时期一度中断了。她把姐姐、姐姐的两个孩子和约翰召集到桌旁，点上一支蜡烛，唱一首赞美诗，朗读《圣经》。 At least, that was the plan. As Cherie played a hymn on YouTube, John wriggled out of his seat and blew out the candle. While she read aloud from Psalm 29, he stood on his chair, propping one foot on the table in a Superman pose. 至少，计划是这样的。当耿朋朋用YouTube播放赞美诗时，约翰从座位上扭下来，吹灭了蜡烛。当她朗读《诗篇》第29篇时，他站在椅子上，一只脚撑在桌面上，摆出超人的姿势。 “You think Jehovah is so awesome. That’s why you’re standing, right?” Cherie said. “Could you please sit down?” “你觉得耶和华太厉害了。所以你才站起来，对吧？”耿朋朋说。“能不能请你坐下？” When he didn’t move, her voice turned firmer: “You’ll break the table. Sit in the chair.” 他没动，她的语气变得更坚定：“你要把桌子弄坏了。坐到椅子上。” She asked him to say a prayer. Still giggling, he complied. 她让他做祷告。他一边咯咯笑，一边照做了。 “Thank you Jesus thank you Dad come home quickly thank you Mom,” he blurted in one breath. “Amen!” “感谢耶稣感谢爸爸快回家感谢妈妈，”他一口气脱口而出。“阿们！” 最近，约翰在泰国交到了第一个朋友，是他幼儿园里的另一个男孩。礼拜结束后，耿朋朋和约翰与家人一起吃午饭。 The next morning, Cherie got up early to write to Yingjia. There was always so much to share. About how John had made a friend and stopped praying to return to Beijing. About how she had lost her temper with the boy, again, and he had bitten his arm until the skin broke. About how he was visibly happier with his aunt and cousins around. 第二天早上，耿朋朋早早起床给高颖佳写信。总有太多事情要分享。比如约翰交了一个朋友，不再祷告求回北京了。比如她又对儿子发了脾气，而他咬自己的手臂，咬到皮肤破了。比如有阿姨和表亲在身边，他明显更开心了。 But then John woke up and called for her. 但这时约翰醒了，喊她过去。 And then it was time to go. 然后就到了该出门的时候。 “Sorry, I’m about to be late. I have to go to work now. John wanted me to keep him company just now, so I couldn’t finish writing,” she wrote. “Love you always.” “抱歉，我快迟到了。我现在得去上班。约翰刚才想让我陪他，所以我没能写完，”她写道。“永远爱你。” 摄影：Lauren DeCicca 王月眉(Vivian Wang)是时报驻纽约记者，报道中国的崛起及雄心如何影响中国国内外民众的生活。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。
content: 王月眉 2026年9月29日 耿朋朋在住处的前院。 On the 308th day after the Chinese police took her husband, Cherie Geng was making dumplings. The smell of a finished batch wafted from the kitchen as she mixed flour and water at her dining table. Her 6-year-old son was busy trading Pokemon figurines with a friend, so Cherie pushed a plate toward the friend’s mom, who had come to drop him off for the play date. 在中国警方带走她丈夫后的第308天，耿朋朋正在包饺子。她在餐桌上和面时，厨房里飘来一阵刚出锅的饺子的香味。她六岁的儿子正忙着和一个小伙伴交换宝可梦玩偶，于是耿朋朋把一盘饺子推向那位小朋友的妈妈——她是送孩子过来玩的。 “This is pretty good — the dough is soft,” the other mom said. “Last time I made dough, it was so hard I felt like I was choking.” “这个挺好吃的——面很软，”那位妈妈说。“我上次和的面特别硬，吃得我都觉得噎得慌。” “I’m not great at it either,” Cherie said. “Normally it’s my husband who likes making dumplings.” He had been a one-man assembly line, sifting flour, mixing filling and folding wrappers. “If we were feeding two or three people, he’d say, ‘You don’t need to do anything.’” “我也不太会，”耿朋朋说道，“平时都是我丈夫喜欢包饺子。”以前，他包起饺子来就像一条一个人的流水线，从筛面粉、拌馅到包饺子，全都不在话下。“要是只做两三个人吃的，他就会说，‘你什么都不用干。’” Now, though, Cherie had to do everything. Her husband, a pastor at one of China’s biggest underground churches, was seized last October by officers who roused him from bed at 2 a.m. Afterward, Cherie, fearing arrest herself, had fled with their son to Thailand. Since then, she had been in charge of not just cooking, but also renting a home, sorting out visas, finding schools and earning an income. She’d had to figure out where she could find authentic Chinese beef noodles, where to buy Chinese picture books. Having just learned to drive in Beijing, she now had to drive on the other side of the road. 可现在，什么都得耿朋朋自己来。她的丈夫是中国规模最大的地下教会之一的一名牧师，去年10月的一天，警察在凌晨2点把他从睡梦中叫醒并带走。之后，耿朋朋担心自己也会被捕，于是带着儿子逃到泰国。从那以后，她不仅要做饭，还得租房、办签证、找学校、挣钱养家。她得弄清楚哪里能吃到正宗的中国牛肉面，哪里可以买到中文绘本。她刚在北京学会开车，现在却得适应靠左行驶。 All this while trying to get her husband out of jail. She spent hours learning the intricacies of Chinese law and trying to craft attention-grabbing social media posts. Most days, it felt like all she could do was explain to her son where his father was. 与此同时，她还得设法营救丈夫出狱。她花了很多时间钻研中国法律的种种细节，还要琢磨怎样写出能引起关注的社交媒体帖子。大多数日子里，她觉得自己能做的只有向儿子解释爸爸去了哪里。 耿朋朋的丈夫高颖佳是中国最大地下教会之一的二号人物。 当耿朋朋带着六岁的儿子约翰逃到泰国时，约翰不太会说英语，在课堂上有些吃力。 The Chinese government’s crackdown on Zion Church was its biggest roundup of Christians in nearly a decade, as the authorities have increasingly tried to shut down religious groups that do not declare loyalty to the ruling Communist Party. In May, President Trump personally asked China’s leader, Xi Jinping, to free the lead pastor, Ezra Jin; Jin was soon released and now lives in the United States . 中国政府 对锡安教会的打压 是近十年来针对基督徒规模最大的一次集中抓捕。近年来，当局越来越严厉地打压那些不愿向执政的共产党宣示效忠的宗教团体。今年5月，特朗普总统亲自请求中国领导人习近平释放锡安教会主任牧师金明日； 不久后，金明日获释，现在生活在美国。 But eight church members remain in detention, including Cherie’s husband, Gao Yingjia. China has signaled that it may sentence them to more than 10 years in prison, and their families are desperately trying to keep attention on their cases. 但仍有八名教会成员遭到羁押，其中包括耿朋朋的丈夫高颖佳。中国已经释放信号，他们可能会被判处十年以上有期徒刑，而他们的家人正拼命让外界持续关注这些案件。 At the same time, they must contend with how the arrests have rippled through their own lives. Most of the relatives who remain free had little public role at the church, and little preparation for what befell them. When Cherie once asked her husband whether they should make a plan in case he was arrested, he replied that they should just place their faith in God. 与此同时，他们还不得不应付亲人被抓给自己的生活带来的连锁冲击。这些仍然自由的家属大多过去在教会里并不担任什么公开角色，对降临在自己身上的一切也几乎毫无准备。有一次，耿朋朋问丈夫，万一他被捕，他们是不是应该提前做个打算。丈夫回答说，他们只需要信靠上帝。 Now, Cherie, 46, had little choice. It wasn’t easy. She was on her own in a part of Thailand she had never been to before, unsure when she might see her home or her husband again. Even here, she didn’t feel totally safe: She slept with a golf club by her bed and didn’t want her specific location published, in case the Chinese police tried to track her down. Her husband’s trial had recently been postponed without explanation, which gave her faint hope that the charges would be dropped and he would be freed. But Cherie also knew that outcome was most likely preordained, and the delay might just mean more time in limbo. 如今，46岁的耿朋朋几乎没有选择。这并不容易。她独自生活在泰国一个以前从未去过的地方，不知道什么时候才能再见到自己的家，也不知道什么时候才能再见到丈夫。即使到了这里，她也不觉得完全安全：睡觉时，她会在床边放一根高尔夫球杆，也不希望报道披露她的具体住处，担心中国警方会设法追踪到她。丈夫的庭审不久前无故延期，这让她燃起了一丝微弱的希望——或许指控会被撤销，他会重获自由。但耿朋朋也明白，结果很可能早已注定，延期或许只意味着这段悬而未决的日子还要继续。 In her hardest moments, Cherie allowed herself to imagine how things might have been different. Before she became a mother and a pastor’s wife, she had earned a Ph.D. in genetics and held a lucrative job at a pharmaceutical company. She could picture a world in which she had never become a Christian, never married a pastor and just lived a comfortable life. 在最艰难的时刻，耿朋朋也会放任自己去想像，如果当初不一样，现在会怎样。在成为母亲和牧师妻子之前，她拿到了遗传学博士学位，并在一家制药公司拥有一份高薪工作。她能在脑海中描绘出另一种人生：自己从未成为基督徒，从未嫁给牧师，只是过着安逸的生活。 为了防身，耿朋朋睡觉时会在床边放一根高尔夫球杆。她儿子常做噩梦，梦见妈妈被抓走。 耿朋朋和约翰在一位朋友陪同下出门去教会。 Still, in some ways her ordeal had made her feel closer to her faith, and her husband, than ever before. Between batches of dumplings, she shared a post on X calling for the pastors’ freedom, and sent a text message to the other pastors’ relatives to confirm a strategy call later that night. There was an irony to her situation: Now, when the burden of being a pastor’s wife was heavier than ever, she was finally doing what Yingjia had always advised her to do, just giving up control and trusting in God. 她还不断祷告。她的处境颇具讽刺意味：如今，当身为牧师妻子的重担比以往任何时候都更沉重时，她终于做到了高颖佳一直建议她做的事——放手，信靠上帝。 Cherie sang quietly as she drove. She decided to put the lyrics in her next letter to Yingjia. 耿朋朋一边开车一边轻声唱着。她决定把歌词写进下一封给高颖佳的信里。 *** *** Cherie made it through her first day of work, but she couldn’t rest yet. After a dinner of steamed buns prepared by her sister, Cherie called a family meeting, a tradition from Beijing that had fallen off in the chaos of leaving China. She gathered her sister, her sister’s two children and John around the table to light a candle, sing a hymn and read the Bible. 耿朋朋熬过了第一天上班，但她还不能休息。吃完姐姐准备的蒸馒头做晚餐后，耿朋朋召集了一次家庭会议——这是在北京时的传统，在离开中国的那段混乱时期一度中断了。她把姐姐、姐姐的两个孩子和约翰召集到桌旁，点上一支蜡烛，唱一首赞美诗，朗读《圣经》。 At least, that was the plan. As Cherie played a hymn on YouTube, John wriggled out of his seat and blew out the candle. While she read aloud from Psalm 29, he stood on his chair, propping one foot on the table in a Superman pose. 至少，计划是这样的。当耿朋朋用YouTube播放赞美诗时，约翰从座位上扭下来，吹灭了蜡烛。当她朗读《诗篇》第29篇时，他站在椅子上，一只脚撑在桌面上，摆出超人的姿势。 “You think Jehovah is so awesome. That’s why you’re standing, right?” Cherie said. “Could you please sit down?” “你觉得耶和华太厉害了。所以你才站起来，对吧？”耿朋朋说。“能不能请你坐下？” When he didn’t move, her voice turned firmer: “You’ll break the table. Sit in the chair.” 他没动，她的语气变得更坚定：“你要把桌子弄坏了。坐到椅子上。” She asked him to say a prayer. Still giggling, he complied. 她让他做祷告。他一边咯咯笑，一边照做了。 “Thank you Jesus thank you Dad come home quickly thank you Mom,” he blurted in one breath. “Amen!” “感谢耶稣感谢爸爸快回家感谢妈妈，”他一口气脱口而出。“阿们！” 最近，约翰在泰国交到了第一个朋友，是他幼儿园里的另一个男孩。 礼拜结束后，耿朋朋和约翰与家人一起吃午饭。 The next morning, Cherie got up early to write to Yingjia. There was always so much to share. About how John had made a friend and stopped praying to return to Beijing. About how she had lost her temper with the boy, again, and he had bitten his arm until the skin broke. About how he was visibly happier with his aunt and cousins around. 第二天早上，耿朋朋早早起床给高颖佳写信。总有太多事情要分享。比如约翰交了一个朋友，不再祷告求回北京了。比如她又对儿子发了脾气，而他咬自己的手臂，咬到皮肤破了。比如有阿姨和表亲在身边，他明显更开心了。 But then John woke up and called for her. 但这时约翰醒了，喊她过去。 And then it was time to go. 然后就到了该出门的时候。 “Sorry, I’m about to be late. I have to go to work now. John wanted me to keep him company just now, so I couldn’t finish writing,” she wrote. “Love you always.” “抱歉，我快迟到了。我现在得去上班。约翰刚才想让我陪他，所以我没能写完，”她写道。“永远爱你。” 摄影：Lauren DeCicca 王月眉( Vivian Wang )是时报驻纽约记者，报道中国的崛起及雄心如何影响中国国内外民众的生活。 翻译：纽约时报中文网 点击查看本文英文版。

title: 一对湾区夫妇被控枪杀跨性别女婿
description: SOUMYA KARLAMANGLA, AMY QIN2026年9月29日40岁的乔纳森·麦金西周六被发现死于一个停车场，身中数枪。停车场位于加州都柏林的都柏林体育场，这是一座体育综合设施和游乐场。 via LinkedIn A Bay Area couple have been accused of shooting and killing their son-in-law in a suburban sports park on Saturday afternoon, the local police said. 当地警方称，一对湾区夫妇被指控于周六下午在郊区一个体育公园枪杀他们的女婿。 The man, Jonathan McKinsey, 40, was found dead with multiple gunshot wounds around 3 p.m. in a parking lot at Dublin Sports Grounds, an athletic complex and playground in Dublin, Calif., about 35 miles east of downtown San Francisco, according to Dublin Police Services. 据都柏林警察局称，这名男子是40岁的乔纳森·麦金西，下午3点左右被发现死于都柏林体育场的停车场，身中数枪。该体育场是加州都柏林的一个体育综合设施和游乐场，位于旧金山市中心以东约35英里（约合55公里）处。 Mr. McKinsey was director of engineering for the games department of The New York Times, according to a company spokesman. Before Mr. McKinsey began working at The Times in 2023, he worked for several tech companies including Splunk, Coursera and Oracle, according to his LinkedIn profile. 据纽约时报公司发言人称，麦金西是公司游戏部门工程总监。根据他的领英个人资料，2023年加入时报之前，他曾在Splunk、Coursera和Oracle等几家科技公司工作。 The authorities arrested Shouyong Zhang and Shili Chen, both 76, in the shooting. They are a married couple who live in Dublin and are the parents of Mr. McKinsey’s wife, the police said. 警方称，当局已就该枪击案逮捕了年龄皆为76岁的张守勇（音）和陈诗丽（音）。他们是一对居住在都柏林的夫妻，是麦金西妻子的父母。 No motive was described by the police for the shooting, but Mr. McKinsey and his wife had a turbulent marriage and were living separately, records show. Each had filed requests for domestic violence restraining orders against the other last year in Alameda County. Mr. McKinsey had also pleaded not guilty last year to two charges of misdemeanor child abuse. 警方没有说明枪击动机，但记录显示麦金西与妻子婚姻破裂，两人已分居。去年，两人都在阿拉米达县申请了对对方的家庭暴力限制令。麦金西去年还对两项轻罪儿童虐待指控表示不认罪。 Mr. McKinsey was a transgender man and accused his wife, Candice Jang, and his in-laws of abusing him because of his identity, according to his filing for a restraining order in December 2025. He said his mother-in-law called him and one of his sons a “pervert” and a “monster” after the boy tried on dresses, and he accused his father-in-law of punching him in the chest while he was recovering from double mastectomy surgery in 2010. 根据麦金西2025年12月提交的限制令申请，他是一名跨性别男性，指控妻子坎迪斯·张和岳父母因他的这一身份而虐待他。他说，岳母在他的一个儿子试穿裙子后，称他和儿子是“变态”和“怪物”；他还指控岳父在2010年他双乳切除术恢复期间拳打他的胸部。 In her October 2025 filing, Ms. Jang said that Mr. McKinsey had grabbed her by the forearms during one argument and dropped her onto the corner of a table, fracturing vertebra in her upper back. Ms. Jang also accused Mr. McKinsey of emotionally abusing her mother. 坎迪斯·张在2025年10月的申请中说，麦金西在一次争吵中抓住她的前臂，令她撞到桌角，导致背部椎骨骨折。她还指控麦金西对她的母亲进行情感虐待。 Efforts to reach Ms. Jang and her lawyer on Monday were unsuccessful. 周一，本报试图联系张女士及其律师未果。 Assad Razawi, a resident of Dublin, said he was outside a grocery store near his car on Saturday at around 3 p.m. on Saturday when he heard what sounded like five or six gunshots coming from the sports park across the street. When he looked over, he said he saw a man drop to the ground in the parking lot and another man and woman walking calmly away from the scene. The San Francisco Chronicle was first to report Mr. Razawi’s account. 都柏林居民阿萨德·拉扎维说，周六下午3点左右，他在杂货店外自己的车旁，听到街对面体育公园传来像是五六声枪响。他看到一名男子在停车场倒地，另一名男子和一名女子平静地离开现场。《旧金山纪事报》最先报道了拉扎维的陈述。 Around the same time, a Dublin police sergeant was driving by the park when he saw a man lying on the ground and stopped to investigate, the local police said. Emergency personnel began arriving after receiving 911 calls from people in the park about the shooting. 当地警方称，大约同一时间，一名都柏林警局警佐开车经过公园，看到一名男子躺在地上，便停车调查。在接到公园内人们关于枪击的911报警后，急救人员开始抵达。 Witnesses directed officers to two individuals standing nearby, whom police identified as Mr. Zhang and Ms. Chen. They are being held without the possibility of bail on suspicion of murder, and detectives are continuing to investigate. They also are being held on suspicion of willful discharge of a firearm with gross negligence; conspiracy; and child endangerment likely to produce great bodily injury or death. It was not clear which children the last booking charge pertained to. 目击者指引警员找到站在附近的两人，警方确认他们是张先生和陈女士。他们因涉嫌谋杀被关押，不得保释，警探正在继续调查。他们还因涉嫌故意开枪并严重疏忽、共谋，以及可能造成严重身体伤害或死亡的儿童危害而被关押。目前不清楚最后一项收押指控涉及的儿童是谁。 They are scheduled to be arraigned on Wednesday. It was unclear whether Mr. Zhang and Ms. Chen had legal representation. 他们定于周三被提审。目前不清楚张先生和陈女士是否有法律代表。 A report from the Dublin Police Services noted that on Oct. 17, 2025, an officer met with Ms. Jang, who said that her husband had struck their 6-year-old “in the face with an open hand.” When officers went to the residence to contact Mr. McKinsey, they discovered a 2-year-old child in an upstairs bedroom who had been left without supervision. The officers say that Mr. McKinsey had left the child alone for over an hour while he went shopping. 都柏林警察局的一份报告指出，一名警员于2025年10月17日见了张女士，她说丈夫“用手掌打了他们六岁孩子的脸”。当警员前往住所联系麦金西时，发现一名两岁儿童被留在楼上卧室，无人监管。警员称，麦金西让孩子独自待了一个多小时，自己去购物。 Mr. McKinsey was later charged in Alameda County Superior Court with two misdemeanor counts of child abuse in connection with the separate incidents. He had pleaded not guilty to both charges and was released from jail on the condition that he complete 12 parenting classes. A pretrial hearing had been scheduled for next month. 鉴于这些本身无关联的事件，麦金西后来在阿拉米达县高等法院被指控两项轻罪儿童虐待。他在对两项指控均不认罪后获释，条件是完成12节育儿课程。审前听证会原定于下个月举行。 In December, Mr. McKinsey filed his own request for a temporary restraining order against his wife, citing years of domestic violence. According to his filing, his wife had recently been granted full custody of the children, and he feared for their safety. That same month, he filed for divorce. 12月，麦金西提交了自己对妻子的临时限制令申请，理由是多年的家庭暴力。根据他的申请，妻子最近获得了孩子的完全监护权，他担心他们的安全。同月，他申请离婚。 Mr. McKinsey said that he had been framed for the October incident in which the couple’s 2-year-old son was found alone. He said that Ms. Jang was responsible for the children during the workweek and that she had not told him before leaving that the child was sleeping in his crib upstairs. “She did this on purpose, to set me up,” he wrote. 麦金西说，在10月这对夫妇的两岁儿子被发现独自一人的事件中，他是被陷害的。他说张女士在工作日负责孩子，她离开前没有告诉他孩子正在楼上婴儿床里睡觉。“她故意这样做，来陷害我，”他写道。 In his filing, he accused his wife of regularly abusing their children and neglecting to properly bathe and feed them. 在申请中，他指控妻子经常虐待孩子，并且没有给他们适当洗澡和喂食的照护。 “When I protested about any of this, she threatened me with harm or said she would call the police and tell them I was hurting our children,” he said in the filing. “当我对此提出抗议时，她威胁要伤害我，或者说她会报警并告诉他们，我在伤害我们的孩子，”他在申请中说。 He said that Ms. Jang had once hit him on the head with a frying pan and forced him to ingest a cockroach. He accused her, on another occasion, of striking him on the head with a mirror, which shattered as he tried to wrest it from her control and severed a tendon and nerve in his hand, requiring surgery and leaving him with a permanent loss of sensation in his thumb. 他说张女士曾用煎锅打他的头，并强迫他吞下一只蟑螂。他还指控她有一次用镜子打他的头，当他试图从她手中夺走镜子时，镜子碎裂，切断了他手部的一条肌腱和神经，需要手术，并导致他拇指感觉永久性丧失。 Kitty Bennett和Georgia Gee对本文有研究贡献。Coral Murphy Marcos自加州海沃德对本文有报道贡献。 Soumya Karlamangla是时报报道加州新闻的记者，常驻旧金山湾区。 Amy Qin是时报美国国内新闻记者，主要报道亚裔美国人社区。 翻译：经雷 点击查看本文英文版。
